Fill the claims in as the work lands. The placeholder is the starting position of a real assessment, so keep it and update it.

docs.title: pacto lock
docs.text:
Resolves the full transitive dependency and reference closure and writes a committed pacto.lock pinning each to its OCI digest. With --check, verifies the existing lock without writing.

pacto lock [dir] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto lock
  pacto lock --update
  pacto lock --update-name auth
  pacto lock --check

Flags:

      --check                     verify pacto.lock is up to date without writing (non-zero exit on drift)
  -h, --help                      help for lock
      --set stringArray           set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --update                    re-resolve dependencies to the newest version within their constraint
      --update-name stringArray   re-resolve only the named dependency, preserving all other pins (repeatable)
  -f, --values stringArray        values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

See Lockfile for the lock model and how .pactoignore keeps a pacto.lock out of a pushed bundle.

docs.title: pacto login
docs.text:
Stores credentials for an OCI registry in ~/.config/pacto/config.json.

pacto login <registry> [flags]

Examples:

  pacto login ghcr.io -u my-username

Flags:

  -h, --help              help for login
  -p, --password string   registry password
  -u, --username string   registry username

Credentials are stored in ~/.config/pacto/config.json (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pacto/config.json), keeping them separate from Docker's configuration.

docs.title: GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io)
docs.text:
For GitHub registries (ghcr.io and docker.pkg.github.com), pacto can reuse credentials from the GitHub CLI, so you can skip pacto login.

If you already have gh installed and authenticated, pacto will use gh auth token to obtain a token transparently. To verify your setup:

# Check if gh is authenticated
gh auth status

# Verify the token is available
gh auth token

To push container images or packages, your token needs the write:packages scope. If you authenticated gh without it, refresh your scopes:

gh auth refresh --scopes write:packages

After this, pacto push oci://ghcr.io/... will work without any additional login step.

If gh is missing or unauthenticated, pacto moves on to the next credential source in the chain.

docs.title: pacto logout
docs.text:
Removes credentials for an OCI registry from ~/.config/pacto/config.json.

pacto logout <registry> [flags]

Examples:

  pacto logout ghcr.io

Flags:

  -h, --help   help for logout

docs.title: pacto mcp
docs.text:
Starts a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing Pacto tools for AI agents. Supports stdio (default) and HTTP transports.

When a bundle reference (local directory or oci:// ref) is given, the server also exposes one executable tool per OpenAPI operation in the bundle's openapi interfaces, plus a pacto_skill tool for any skills/*.md domain knowledge. Read-only (GET/HEAD) operations are exposed by default; pass --allow-writes to expose mutating operations.

With --root, the server exposes a read-only contract catalog: the given roots plus their dependency closure, resolved once at startup and then frozen, so the session keeps its startup view even when a registry tag moves. Roots that fail to resolve stay visible as partial knowledge. The catalog grants no authorization and executes nothing.

With --fleet, the server exposes the read-only operational-graph query tools over one snapshot. The shared fleet source flags (--local, --target-state, --evidence-url, --traces, --oci, --cache, --k8s, --namespace and --freshness) compose that snapshot and are read in --fleet mode only.

With --delivery, the server exposes the Pacto delivery tools (pacto_delivery_*) over the ambient cluster: operation types, plan, get, explain, history, blame, undo plans and record checks, plus propose and cancel only when the apiserver says the caller is an agent (a service account, or an agent by the identity policy Pacto delivery publishes). It has no approve tool.

Over HTTP, --auth-issuer and --resource make every request carry a bearer token the server verifies (issuer, audience, expiry) and publish protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728); a bind beyond loopback needs them and refuses --auth and --allow-writes, which would lend this process's service credential to every caller. With --delivery the server then exchanges each caller's token for one the apiserver accepts (RFC 8693, --exchange-client-id) and builds the tools for that caller on every request, so an agent proposes as itself and a person gets the read-only tools. With --fleet the server names each caller with the claim mapping (--oidc-username-claim, --oidc-username-prefix, --oidc-groups-claim and --oidc-groups-prefix) and asks Kubernetes RBAC about that user; the API server does not confirm it, so the mapping must match its claimMappings.

With --publish, the authoring server also exposes pacto_publish_plan and pacto_publish, which publish a contract's version exactly as pacto publish does, with this process's registry credentials.

A bundle reference, --root, --fleet, --delivery and --publish select different servers and cannot be combined.

pacto mcp [bundle-ref] [flags]

Examples:

  # Start MCP server over stdio (default)
  pacto mcp

  # Start MCP server over HTTP
  pacto mcp -t http

  # Expose a bundle's OpenAPI operations as agent tools
  pacto mcp ./my-service --base-url https://api.example.com

  # Include mutating operations and an auth credential
  pacto mcp oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc:1.0.0 --base-url https://api.example.com \
    --auth bearerAuth=$TOKEN --allow-writes

  # Expose a contract catalog discovered from explicit roots
  pacto mcp --root oci://ghcr.io/acme/platform:1.4.0 --root ./experimental-platform

Flags:

      --allow-writes                  expose mutating operations (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) as tools
      --audience string               with --auth-issuer: the audience incoming tokens must carry (default --resource)
      --auth stringArray              credential for a security scheme as name=value (repeatable)
      --auth-issuer string            OpenID issuer whose bearer tokens every HTTP request must carry
      --base-url string               base URL for live invocation (overrides the OpenAPI servers[] URL)
      --cache                         include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --delivery                      expose the Pacto delivery tools over the ambient cluster
      --delivery-namespace string     in --delivery mode: namespace Pacto delivery runs in, whose published identity policy (agent, break-glass and human groups, team prefix) says who is an agent and who may answer (default "pacto-delivery")
      --delivery-trust string         in --delivery mode: the trust config delivery records are verified with (the recorder's PEM public key or a YAML trust config; default $PACTO_DELIVERY_TRUST)
      --evidence-url stringArray      base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --exchange-audience string      with --delivery over HTTP: the audience to exchange for, one the apiserver accepts (default "pacto-cli")
      --exchange-client-id string     with --delivery over HTTP: the server's own OAuth client, which exchanges each caller's token for the cluster (RFC 8693); its secret comes from PACTO_MCP_EXCHANGE_CLIENT_SECRET
      --fleet                         expose read-only operational-graph (fleet) query tools
      --freshness duration            mark target evidence older than this as stale (0 disables)
  -h, --help                          help for mcp
      --host string                   bind address for HTTP transport; beyond loopback it needs --auth-issuer (default "127.0.0.1")
      --k8s                           include live Pacto CRs from the current Kubernetes cluster as targets
      --local stringArray             local bundle root(s) to scan (repeatable) (default [.])
      --namespace string              namespace to read Pacto CRs from with --k8s (empty = all namespaces)
      --oci stringArray               registry reference to include as a published-baseline revision (repeatable)
      --oidc-groups-claim string      ID token claim the API server takes the groups from; must match its claim mapping (default groups)
      --oidc-groups-prefix string     prefix the API server puts before every group; must match its claim mapping
      --oidc-username-claim string    ID token claim the API server takes the username from; must match its claim mapping (default sub)
      --oidc-username-prefix string   prefix the API server puts before the username; must match its claim mapping (default the issuer URL and #, none for the email claim; - for none)
      --port int                      port for HTTP transport (default 8585)
      --publish                       expose pacto_publish_plan and pacto_publish beside the authoring tools
      --resource string               with --auth-issuer: this endpoint's URL as clients reach it, served as protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728)
      --root stringArray              contract root to discover a read-only catalog from: a local bundle path or an oci:// reference (repeatable)
      --target-state stringArray      offline target-state fixture file(s) supplying targets, for demos and tests; production targets arrive as signed EvidenceSets (repeatable)
      --traces stringArray            OTLP/JSON trace file supplying runtime-observed dependency edges, folded into the snapshot as observed relationships (repeatable)
  -t, --transport string              transport type: stdio or http (default "stdio")

The default server exposes the four authoring tools below. A bundle reference and four flags select a different server, each with its own tools. See Server modes after this table:

Tool Description pacto_create Create a new contract from intent-level inputs (name, description, interfaces, runtime semantics). Supports dry run. pacto_edit Edit an existing contract: add or remove interfaces and dependencies, change runtime, update metadata. Supports dry run. pacto_check Validate a contract and return errors, warnings and actionable improvement suggestions. pacto_schema Return the Pacto format explanation and full JSON Schema reference.

These four authoring tools operate on local contract directories (they read and write pacto.yaml on disk) and accept no oci:// refs.

docs.title: Server modes
docs.text:
The default server exposes the authoring tools above. A bundle reference, --root, --fleet, --publish and --delivery each select a different server. Passing more than one is an error:

Invocation Server pacto mcp Authoring tools. pacto mcp <bundle-ref> Authoring tools plus the bundle's OpenAPI operations as executable agent tools, alongside a pacto_skill tool for any bundled skills. pacto mcp --fleet Authoring tools plus read-only operational-graph query tools. pacto mcp --publish Authoring tools plus pacto_publish_plan and pacto_publish, which publish a version to your registry. Stdio only. pacto mcp --delivery Authoring tools plus the delivery tools over the cluster your kubeconfig points at: read delivery state and, for an agent, ask for or cancel a change. There is no approve tool. pacto mcp --root <ref> [--root <ref>] A read-only contract catalog discovered from the named roots. Catalog mode registers only catalog tools, and none of them writes to disk.

--root is repeatable and takes a local bundle directory or an oci:// reference. The roots and their dependency closure are resolved once, at startup, through the same reference parsing, credentials and cache the rest of the CLI uses; after that the session is frozen, so every answer reflects startup state even if a registry tag moves. A root that fails to resolve stays visible with a classified reason, and the catalog reports itself as partial. The catalog reads only the named roots and their closure, never refreshes and persists nothing.

docs.title: Fleet tool arguments
docs.text:
The arguments each fleet query tool takes. Arguments are optional unless marked:

Tool Arguments pacto_fleet_search text, owner, status, compliance, workload, scope, source, ready, not_ready, has_capability, has_dependency, limit pacto_fleet_get service (a logical service) or target (an operational target by key or name) pacto_fleet_graph service, revision or target to root the traversal, then direction, transitive and max_depth (0 = unlimited) pacto_fleet_status needs_attention for every category, or any of invalid, non_compliant, unknown, stale, unresolved_deps, unsatisfied_ranges, missing_readiness; plus limit. No category, including empty input, reports every category pacto_fleet_explain subject (required): a service name or a target key or name pacto_impact old_ref and new_ref (both required), plus include_observed and traces

Argument names differ from flag names: the substring filter is text. Every tool above closes its schema, so an unknown argument is an error.

See MCP Integration for setup and the MCP reference for serving a bundle's operations as tools and the catalog surface.

docs.title: pacto otel
docs.text:
Observe runtime dependencies from OpenTelemetry traces

pacto otel [flags]

Flags:

  -h, --help   help for otel

docs.title: pacto otel observe
docs.text:
Reads an OTLP/JSON trace export and derives the service dependency edges its outbound spans prove. By default it prints the observed edges as text; add --output-format json for machine-readable output. With --evidence it emits one EvidenceSet per calling service as a JSON array. Each set's ContractRef is empty because traces carry no contract revision. pacto evidence sign reads one EvidenceSet from a file, so write the array out, split it and set each ContractRef to the revision it describes before signing (pacto evidence sign) and reporting (pacto evidence send).

pacto otel observe <traces.json> [flags]

Examples:

  pacto otel observe traces.json
  pacto otel observe traces.json --evidence --output-format json > sets.json

Flags:

      --evidence        emit signable EvidenceSets instead of raw edges
  -h, --help            help for observe
      --source string   collector/source name recorded as provenance (default "otel")

docs.title: pacto pack
docs.text:
Validates the contract in the given directory and creates a tar.gz archive of the bundle, ready for distribution.

pacto pack [dir] [flags]

Examples:

  pacto pack my-service

Flags:

  -h, --help                 help for pack
  -o, --output string        output file path (default: <name>-<version>.tar.gz)
      --set stringArray      set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
  -f, --values stringArray   values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

The contract is validated before packing. If validation fails, no archive is created.

Files matched by .pactoignore are excluded from the archive. See Packaging ignore.

docs.title: pacto publish
docs.text:
Publishes every artifact the contract's publish section declares (pactoVersion 2.1), the contract bundle and the deploy artifact Flux applies, all tagged with service.version. Docker or the declared command builds. Pacto pushes each artifact to a new tag, signs every digest with Sigstore (built in) and attaches the SBOM files the build wrote. A breaking change since the last published version is refused below a major bump (a minor before 1.0).

--plan shows what is missing and changes nothing. Running publish again from the same commit finishes what is missing and changes nothing else. --propose hands the deploy artifact to Pacto delivery as a promote on a Stage, once the Stage records it as published, meaning Flux polled the candidate OCIRepository and verified the signature. It waits up to --propose-timeout for that.

pacto publish [dir] [flags]

Examples:

  # What would be published, and what refuses it
  pacto publish --plan

  # The same, for the contract in ./payments
  pacto publish --plan ./payments

  # Publish, then propose the version on the test Stage
  pacto publish --propose test/payments

Flags:

  -h, --help                       help for publish
  -p, --path string                path to contract directory, the same as [dir] (default: current directory)
      --plan                       show what is missing and what refuses it; change nothing
      --propose string             after publishing, propose the deploy artifact on <namespace>/<stage> (needs delivery.enabled on the pacto-operator chart)
      --propose-timeout duration   how long --propose waits for the Stage to record the version as published (default 10m0s)
      --revision string            source revision stamped on every artifact (default: the git commit of the contract directory, which must have no uncommitted changes)
      --set stringArray            set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --values stringArray         values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

docs.title: pacto pull
docs.text:
Pulls a contract bundle from the specified OCI reference and extracts it to a local directory.

pacto pull <ref> [flags]

Examples:

  # Pull a specific version
  pacto pull oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto:1.0.0

  # Pull the latest available version
  pacto pull oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto

Flags:

  -h, --help            help for pull
  -o, --output string   output directory (default: service name)

docs.title: pacto push
docs.text:
Validates the contract (including remote policy and config refs), builds an OCI artifact and pushes it to the specified registry reference. Pushing the same content again succeeds without writing anything; different content under an existing reference is refused unless --force.

pacto push <ref> [flags]

Examples:

  # Push with auto-tag (uses contract version)
  pacto push oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto -p my-service

  # Push with explicit tag
  pacto push oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto:latest -p my-service

  # Force overwrite an existing artifact
  pacto push oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto -p my-service --force

Flags:

  -f, --force                overwrite existing artifact in registry
  -h, --help                 help for push
  -p, --path string          path to contract directory (default: current directory)
      --set stringArray      set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
      --values stringArray   values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

If the tag already holds the same content, pacto push succeeds and writes nothing. If it holds different content, pacto push refuses with a non-zero exit and writes nothing. Use --force to overwrite.

--values has no -f shorthand on push

On every other override-taking command -f is the shorthand for --values. On pacto push, -f is --force, so --values must be spelled out in full here.

docs.title: pacto run
docs.text:
Starts the command and watches the TCP sockets of its whole process tree: the interfaces bound with --bind must be listened on, the dependencies bound with --dep reached. Every --interval it prints the contract's compliance and findings in --output-format; once the command exits it prints a final round from the last view taken while the command ran, and exits with the command's exit code. With --fail-on it exits 1 instead of 0 when the final verdict is that bad or worse.

The command runs in a process group of its own, so a Ctrl-C reaches it once. When pacto run owns the terminal, the command's group takes it over: it reads the terminal and gets Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z straight from it, and pacto run takes the terminal back once it exits. Otherwise SIGINT and SIGTERM sent to pacto run are passed on to the command's whole group.

Pacto leaves the command's stdin, stdout and stderr untouched. Rounds go to stderr, each in a single write, or with --report to a file: the file is truncated when the run starts and every round is appended to it in a single write, so a reader following it sees whole rounds (with json, one object per line).

With root (or BPF, PERFMON, SYS_PTRACE and write access to its own cgroup) on Linux 5.11 or later with BTF and cgroup v2 (or 5.8 or later with BTF and root or CAP_SYS_RESOURCE), the command starts inside a new cgroup pacto-run-<pid> and an eBPF program sees every listener and every connection outcome of the tree, failures included (collector pacto-run+ebpf). Otherwise it falls back to polling /proc every second and says so (collector pacto-run): listeners are seen in full, so a missing one is still confirmed, but a connection is seen only while it is open at a poll and a failed connection never, so a dependency is reported reachable or unknown, never unreachable. If the program attached but the command cannot start inside the new cgroup, the run falls back to polling too and says so. Elsewhere than Linux the command runs unobserved and every runtime assertion is unsupported.

A negative is reported once it persists for --stabilization-window. Health and metrics capabilities are probed on --host at their bound interface's port. With --evidence-url every round is also signed and sent to an Evidence Server, which needs the contract pinned as oci://...@sha256:<digest>.

pacto run --contract <dir|oci ref> [flags] -- command [args...]

Examples:

  pacto run --contract ./payments --bind api=8080 --dep postgres=127.0.0.1:5432 -- ./payments-server
  pacto run --contract oci://ghcr.io/acme/payments:1.4.0 --bind api=8080 --fail-on noncompliant \
    --stabilization-window 30s --output-format json --report rounds.jsonl -- java -jar payments.jar

Flags:

      --bind stringArray                interface=port the command serves the interface on (repeatable)
      --cgroup-root string              cgroup v2 directory the session cgroup is created in (default: the caller's own cgroup under /sys/fs/cgroup)
      --contract string                 contract bundle directory or oci:// reference (required)
      --dep stringArray                 dependency=host:port the command reaches the dependency at (repeatable)
      --enable-probing                  also probe the wire protocol of every interface found listening
      --evidence-key string             private key file envelopes are signed with
      --evidence-key-id string          key id (must match the server's trust entry)
      --evidence-producer string        producer id
      --evidence-url string             Evidence Server base URL
      --fail-on string                  exit 1 when the command exits 0 but the final verdict is this bad or worse: one of [none noncompliant unknown] (default "none")
  -h, --help                            help for run
      --host string                     address capability and protocol probes dial (default "127.0.0.1")
      --interval duration               how often a round is evaluated and printed (whole seconds) (default 10s)
      --proc-root string                where /proc is mounted (default "/proc")
      --report string                   file every round is appended to instead of stderr (truncated when the run starts)
      --ringbuf-size uint32             kernel ring buffer size in bytes; a power of two and a multiple of the page size (default 262144)
      --stabilization-window duration   how long a negative must persist before it is reported (default 2m0s)

docs.title: pacto tui
docs.text:
Opens a full-screen terminal UI over the same fleet snapshot pacto fleet queries. Navigate services, revisions, targets, owners and sources, then run pacto's verbs against the selection, which becomes the command's argument.

Read verbs run in-process against the loaded snapshot. Write verbs shell out to this same binary so they own the terminal, and every one of them asks for confirmation first. Pass --read-only to hide the write verbs entirely.

Requires an interactive terminal. In a pipeline or CI, use the plain commands.

pacto tui [flags]

Examples:

  # Browse the local fleet
  pacto tui --local .

  # Browse a live cluster plus the local bundles, without write verbs
  pacto tui --local . --k8s --read-only

Flags:

      --cache                      include every bundle in the local OCI cache as an offline baseline revision
      --evidence-url stringArray   base URL of an Evidence Server to consume its read-only operational-graph contribution over HTTP (repeatable)
      --freshness duration         mark target evidence older than this as stale (0 disables)
  -h, --help                       help for tui
      --k8s                        include live Pacto CRs from the current Kubernetes cluster as targets
      --local stringArray          local bundle root(s) to scan (repeatable) (default [.])
      --namespace string           namespace to read Pacto CRs from with --k8s (empty = all namespaces)
      --oci stringArray            registry reference to include as a published-baseline revision (repeatable)
      --read-only                  hide every write verb
      --root stringArray           contract root whose whole dependency closure joins the snapshot: a local bundle path or an oci:// reference (repeatable)
      --target-state stringArray   offline target-state fixture file(s) supplying targets, for demos and tests; production targets arrive as signed EvidenceSets (repeatable)
      --traces stringArray         OTLP/JSON trace file supplying runtime-observed dependency edges, folded into the snapshot as observed relationships (repeatable)

docs.title: pacto update
docs.text:
Downloads and installs the specified version of pacto. If no version is given, updates to the latest release.

pacto update [version] [flags]

Examples:

  # Update to the latest release
  pacto update

  # Update to a specific version
  pacto update v1.1.0

Flags:

  -h, --help   help for update

Note

pacto update works only on release builds. If you built from source without version injection, install a release build first.

docs.title: Update notifications
docs.text:
When a newer version is available, pacto displays a notification after any command:

A new version of pacto is available: v1.0.0 -> v1.2.0
Run 'pacto update' to update.

The check runs asynchronously and adds no latency. Results are cached for 24 hours in ~/.config/pacto/update-check.json.

Notifications are suppressed when:

  • Running a dev build
  • Using --output-format json or --output-format markdown (the notice shows only for text output)
  • The PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 environment variable is set

docs.title: pacto validate
docs.text:
Validates a pacto.yaml in the given directory (or oci:// reference) against the specification, running the three validation layers: structural, cross-field and policy.

The output has one PASS, FAIL or SKIP line per stage, in order: load, lock, structural, cross-field, policy, environments, guarantees, readiness and closure. The environments stage checks each environment's file against the schema of every configuration it names. Each error sits under its stage with its file:line:column when Pacto can locate it. A failed load or lock stage skips every stage after it, and a failed structural or cross-field stage skips the stages after it up to policy. Any failed stage skips environments. The guarantees, readiness and closure stages run even when an earlier stage fails. The last line, Next:, names the one command to run now. With --output-format json the same comes as stages and next.

pacto validate [dir | oci://ref] [flags]

Examples:

  # Validate a local contract
  pacto validate my-service

  # Validate from current directory
  pacto validate

  # Validate from an OCI registry
  pacto validate oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto:1.0.0

  # JSON output
  pacto validate --output-format json my-service

  # Also check the readiness gate (fail if score < minScore)
  pacto validate --readiness my-service

  # Also check every dependency against this contract's policies
  pacto validate --closure my-service

Flags:

      --closure              also check every contract in the dependency closure against the policies this contract resolves. Fails when a dependency cannot be resolved and warns about deprecated interfaces of direct dependencies. Fetches each dependency once
  -h, --help                 help for validate
      --readiness            also check the readiness gate: fail if the derived readiness score is below the declared (or default 100) minScore. Opt-in because gate evaluation is time-dependent (check expiry is compared against the run time), which would otherwise make plain validation non-deterministic
      --set stringArray      set a contract value (e.g. --set service.version=2.0.0)
  -f, --values stringArray   values file to merge into the contract (can be repeated; last wins)

The --readiness gate is opt-in because it is time-dependent: it compares the assessment's single readiness.expires date against the run time, which would make plain validate non-deterministic. Expiry is declared once for the whole assessment. Individual claims carry no expires field, and adding one fails to load with PARSE_ERROR. Without the flag, validation checks the contract's structure and rules. It still checks the shape of readiness claims and skips the freshness gate. See the readiness reference for the score and gate semantics.

A contract with a mistyped value fails like this:

svc is invalid
PASS load
SKIP lock         no pacto.lock
FAIL structural
  svc/pacto.yaml:6:1: ERROR [SCHEMA_VIOLATION] workload: at '/workload': value must be one of 'service', 'job', 'scheduled' (did you mean "service"?)
SKIP cross-field  structural failed
SKIP policy       structural failed
SKIP environments structural failed
SKIP guarantees   no dependency declares requires
SKIP readiness    not requested (--readiness)
SKIP closure      not requested (--closure)
Next: fix workload at svc/pacto.yaml:6:1 [SCHEMA_VIOLATION], then run pacto validate svc

Errors within a stage are listed in file order. An unknown field or an enum value close to a known one carries a did you mean hint. A failed lock stage names the pacto lock command that repairs it. When every stage passes, Next is pacto impact PUBLISHED_REF <dir>, which shows the services the change breaks; replace PUBLISHED_REF with the oci:// reference of the version you run today. In JSON, stages lists each stage with its status, reason and errors, each error carries line and column when known, file is the file they point into, and next holds the command. errors and warnings still list every stage's findings. With --set or -f an error in pacto.yaml carries no line or column, because those flags validate a merged document whose lines differ from the file. An error in an environment's file keeps them.

Exit code: Non-zero if validation fails.

docs.title: pacto version
docs.text:
Prints the current pacto version.

pacto version [flags]

Examples:

  pacto version

Flags:

  -h, --help   help for version

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Boolean variables are parsed the way Go parses a boolean: 1, t, T, true, TRUE and True enable them and 0, f, F, false, FALSE and False disable them. Any other value, including yes and on, reads as off with no warning. The two opt-outs PACTO_NO_ANIM and PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK are the exception: for them any other non-empty value reads as on.

Variable Description PACTO_CACHE_DIR Cache directory for the pacto dashboard bundle scan. The core CLI cache location is controlled by XDG_CACHE_HOME (see below). PACTO_NO_CACHE Boolean. Disable OCI bundle caching (equivalent to --no-cache) PACTO_NO_ANIM Boolean. Disables spinners and animations (equivalent to --no-anim). PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK Boolean. Disables automatic update checks. PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME Registry username for authentication PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD Registry password for authentication PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN Registry token for authentication PACTO_INSECURE_REGISTRIES Comma-separated registry hosts that Pacto reaches over plain HTTP. It applies to every registry access: pacto push, pacto pull, dependency and policy resolution and the Evidence Server. Scoped per host, so HTTPS registries are unaffected. Loopback hosts use plain HTTP without being listed. Use it only for a controlled in-cluster registry: it disables transport encryption, so credentials and payloads travel in the clear. PACTO_EVIDENCE_SOURCE_URL Base URL of an Evidence Server whose read-only operational-graph contribution pacto dashboard should consume. The operator sets it when it wires a managed Evidence Server. Unset means no evidence source configured, which the dashboard reports separately from an unavailable source. XDG_CONFIG_HOME Override config directory (default: ~/.config). Affects pacto login credentials and update check cache XDG_CACHE_HOME Override cache directory (default: ~/.cache). Affects OCI bundle cache location

docs.title: Dashboard environment variables
docs.text:
The following variables configure the dashboard when set (see also Dashboard Container). Each mirrors the flag named beside it: an explicitly passed flag wins, and otherwise the variable overrides that flag's default.

Variable Flag Description PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO (positional args) Comma-separated OCI repositories, used only when no positional oci:// argument is given PACTO_DASHBOARD_HOST --host Bind address (default: 127.0.0.1) PACTO_DASHBOARD_PORT --port HTTP port (default: 3000) PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE --namespace Kubernetes namespace filter (empty = all) PACTO_DASHBOARD_CORS_ORIGIN --cors-origin One explicit origin allowed to call the API. Unset means same-origin only. PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES --traces OTLP/JSON trace files to fold observed dependencies from PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES --trace-source Named offline trace sources as NAME=PATH, where NAME is the source's identity (what the fleet, the API and the dashboard's Data Source list call it) and PATH is the trace file location. Identity and location are separate, so reordering the configuration or moving the file keeps the source's name. Two sources whose files share a basename stay two sources. A name must be unique across every Data Source the dashboard assembles.

The two list variables split on whitespace

PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES and PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES go through the same generic flag binding as every other dashboard variable, which splits a multi-valued string on spaces. PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES="a.json b.json" supplies two files; PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES=a.json,b.json supplies one, named a.json,b.json. PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO is read directly and splits on commas.

The dashboard starts either way: it skips a trace file it cannot read, so the symptom is missing observed dependencies with no error. Check the snapshot's reported limitations if the operational graph looks emptier than you expect.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Pacto follows this credential resolution chain:

  1. Environment variables (PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, or PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME + PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD)
  2. Pacto config (~/.config/pacto/config.json, written by pacto login, which persists --username and --password)
  3. GitHub CLI (gh auth token, for ghcr.io and docker.pkg.github.com only)
  4. Docker config (~/.docker/config.json) and credential helpers (including cloud-registry helpers for ECR, GCR and ACR)
  5. Anonymous fallback

For GitHub registries, step 3 means you can skip pacto login entirely if you have gh authenticated with the write:packages scope (see pacto login above).

Pacto stores no credentials in contract files.

docs.title: How Pacto relates to other tools
docs.text:
Pacto composes the interface tools it sits between, such as OpenAPI and config schemas, and complements the deploy tools, such as Helm and Terraform. Its core makes no deployment decisions. The opt-in delivery component decides which version runs where and leaves applying it to Flux or Argo CD.

This page grades Pacto and several nearby projects on the same criteria. Reviewed on 2026-10-29. Maintainers review this page at every minor release. These projects move fast, so check the source page before you rely on a cell.

docs.title: Criteria
docs.text:
Each column asks one question:

  • Versioned artifact: the tool publishes the service description as an immutable, versioned artifact that others pull, such as an OCI image. Versioned snapshots that stay inside the tool are Partial.
  • Semantic diff: the tool classifies a change by its compatibility impact. A line-based text diff is Partial.
  • Dependency graph: the tool records which services depend on which. Dependencies between platform packages, or inside one application, are Partial.
  • Transitive policy: the platform's rules follow every policy reference, fail closed and are evaluated across the dependency closure. Following the references without evaluating the closure is Partial.
  • Runtime verify: the tool checks running workloads against an independently declared contract. Reconciling toward the tool's own desired state is Partial.
  • Deploys?: the tool applies workloads itself.

A cell holds ✅ for first-class, Partial for adjacent or limited and a dash (—) when the source page covers the area and describes no such feature. A cell holds "not verified" when the source page alone does not settle it.

docs.title: The table
docs.text:
Versioned artifact Semantic diff Dependency graph Transitive policy Runtime verify Deploys? Source Score not verified not verified Partial not verified not verified No Score specification Crossplane Configuration ✅ not verified Partial not verified Partial Yes Configurations KubeVela Partial Partial not verified not verified not verified Yes Version control Kratix Partial not verified Partial not verified not verified Yes Promise reference Kargo Partial not verified — not verified not verified No Core concepts Pacto ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ (opt-in) ✅ No (delivery promotes, alpha) This site

What each source page shows:

  • Score: a Score file describes one workload. Its resources are evaluated as an acyclic graph at deploy time, and a Score implementation turns the file into platform configuration.
  • Crossplane: a Configuration is a versioned OCI package that lists the packages it depends on with version constraints. Crossplane installs and reconciles its contents and reports them Healthy.
  • KubeVela: an ApplicationRevision keeps a snapshot of each published version, vela live-diff prints a line diff between the edited application and its current revision and KubeVela rolls back to a past revision.
  • Kratix: Kratix keeps each Promise version as a Promise Revision, a Promise lists the Promises it requires and Kratix schedules resources to matching Destinations.
  • Kargo: Freight is a Kargo resource that references specific revisions of images, charts and commits. Stages form a promotion pipeline, and a GitOps agent such as Argo CD does the deploying.

docs.title: Pacto's own row
docs.text:
We graded our own row on the same criteria:

  • Transitive policy is ✅ and opt-in. Pacto follows policy references from one policy contract to the next and fails closed when one cannot be resolved. By default it checks the policies against the root contract only. pacto validate --closure also checks every contract in the dependency closure against them, and fails when a dependency cannot be resolved. The flag is on pacto validate only. See Dependency closure.
  • Semantic diff classifies each change as non-breaking, potentially breaking or breaking (diff).
  • Runtime verify compares running workloads with the contract (runtime conformance).
  • Deploys? Pacto's core deploys nothing. Delivery, which is alpha, moves the version digest on a Flux or Argo CD source, and Flux or Argo CD applies it (delivery).

Radius, Backstage and Port were in an earlier version of this table. Their rows are out until a source page settles most of their cells.

docs.title: Dashboard Container
docs.text: Run the Pacto dashboard, a web UI for your services, their contracts, dependencies and compliance, as a container. It is the same server as pacto dashboard in the CLI, packaged for Docker and Kubernetes.

docs.title: Image
docs.text:
ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:<version>

The tag matches the Pacto release version, without a v prefix. The image has no latest tag, so swap the pinned version below for the release you want. The image is signed keylessly; verify it with the command in Supply chain.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Every docker run here publishes to 127.0.0.1 on purpose: the image sets --host 0.0.0.0 and the dashboard has no authentication by default.

# Run with OCI registry sources
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO=ghcr.io/org/svc-a,ghcr.io/org/svc-b \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.4.0

# Run with registry authentication
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO=ghcr.io/org/svc-a \
  -e PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=ghp_xxx \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.4.0

To build the image from a checkout instead, make docker-build and make docker-run tag it with the version derived from your git state.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Variable Description Default PACTO_DASHBOARD_HOST Bind address for the server 0.0.0.0 (in image), 127.0.0.1 (CLI) PACTO_DASHBOARD_PORT HTTP server port 3000 PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE Kubernetes namespace filter (empty = all) "" PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO Comma-separated OCI repositories to scan "" PACTO_DASHBOARD_CORS_ORIGIN Trusted cross-origin allowed to call the API "" (same-origin only) PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACES Offline OTLP/JSON trace exports to fold observed dependencies from. Space-separated list of paths "" PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_ISSUER_URL Identity provider people sign in with before the dashboard shows anything; every view then follows their Kubernetes RBAC (also _CLIENT_ID, _CLIENT_SECRET, _REDIRECT_URL, _EXTRA_SCOPES, _DISPLAY_NAME for the provider's name on the sign-in button and the claim mapping, see dashboard authentication) "" (no sign-in) PACTO_DASHBOARD_TOKEN_LOGIN true lets people sign in by pasting a Kubernetes bearer token false PACTO_DASHBOARD_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT, PACTO_DASHBOARD_SESSION_MAX_AGE How long a session lasts idle and in all 1h, 12h PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES The same input with a stable identity per file: space-separated NAME=PATH entries, where NAME is the Data Source name the API and UI show "" PACTO_CACHE_DIR Directory the dashboard scans for cached OCI bundles (read side) /home/pacto/.cache/pacto/oci PACTO_NO_CACHE Disable OCI bundle caching (1) 0 PACTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK Disable update checks (1) 1 (set in image) PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME Registry authentication username "" PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD Registry authentication password "" PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN Registry authentication token ""

Most PACTO_DASHBOARD_* variables map to the CLI flag of the same name. Two are different: PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO is the repository positional argument, and PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES maps to --trace-source, singular.

The two trace variables let the dashboard learn which services really call each other, from trace files. Pacto has no OpenTelemetry (OTLP) receiver, so you export traces to files and mount them in. Each file becomes a named observation source. Under Kubernetes the operator-managed dashboard sets PACTO_DASHBOARD_TRACE_SOURCES for you from dashboard.observation.sources. See offline trace sources.

PACTO_CACHE_DIR sets only where the dashboard reads cached bundles. It writes them under XDG_CACHE_HOME. To keep the cache, mount a volume at ~/.cache/pacto/oci. The defaults line up because the image sets HOME=/home/pacto. The Kubernetes example below mounts an emptyDir there instead, so its cache is rebuilt on every restart. The CLI reference lists every variable.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
The dashboard auto-detects its sources at startup. The container-specific bindings are:

  • oci: PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO is set, or repositories are discovered from Kubernetes resolvedRef fields. Supplies bundles, version history, interfaces and diffs.
  • cache: the on-disk OCI cache, surfaced as its own source only as an offline baseline when no registry is configured.
  • k8s: a kubeconfig is mounted, or the container runs in-cluster. Supplies runtime state from the Pacto operator.
  • local: a pacto.yaml is found in the working directory (mount via volume).

docs.title: Kubernetes + OCI hybrid mode
docs.text: When the Kubernetes source is on and the operator fills status.contract.resolvedRef, the dashboard finds the contract repositories by itself. You get what is running from the operator and the contracts from the registry. If a registry is unreachable, or private and not logged in, the dashboard quietly falls back to Kubernetes only: no version history, interfaces, schemas or diffs.

docs.title: Mounting the k8s and local sources
docs.text:
Both arrive as volumes; inside a cluster the in-cluster config is used automatically, with no kubeconfig mount:

# k8s: a kubeconfig, scoped to one namespace
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -v ~/.kube/config:/home/pacto/.kube/config:ro \
  -e PACTO_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE=production \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.4.0

# local: a contract directory
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -v /path/to/contracts:/data:ro \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.4.0 dashboard /data

docs.title: Operational Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoint Description GET /health Returns {"status": "ok", "version": "..."}. Use for liveness and readiness probes. GET /metrics Returns {"serviceCount": N, "sourceCount": N}. GET /openapi.json OpenAPI 3.1 specification (includes a server URL matching the bind address). Also served as /openapi.yaml, and downgraded to OpenAPI 3.0.3 at /openapi-3.0.json. GET /docs Interactive API documentation.

/openapi on its own is a prefix and returns 404. The image also carries a Docker HEALTHCHECK polling /health every 10 seconds.

The status filters of /api/fleet/services, /api/fleet/entities and /api/fleet/attention and the comma-separated kinds filter of /api/fleet/entities are enums checked item by item: an unknown value or an empty item such as a trailing comma gets a 422 that names the parameter, for example query.kinds[1].

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Keep the dashboard private unless sign-in protects it

By default the dashboard has no login, API key or authorization. Anyone who can reach the port reads every contract, dependency and compliance result, and can make the container pull from your registries. Publish it to 127.0.0.1 (-p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000), put an authenticating proxy in front of it, or configure sign-in with PACTO_DASHBOARD_OIDC_ISSUER_URL. The protections below defend against CSRF and resource exhaustion. They give no access control against a client that reaches the port.

A few endpoints mutate local state (POST /api/resolve, POST /api/versions and POST /api/refresh pull and cache OCI artifacts). Against those:

  • Same-origin only by default. No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is emitted and cross-origin mutating requests get a 403, so a malicious page in your browser cannot drive the dashboard. The bundled UI is unaffected.
  • Explicit cross-origin opt-in. --cors-origin https://your-app (or PACTO_DASHBOARD_CORS_ORIGIN) allows one trusted cross-origin client.
  • HTTP timeouts guard against slow-client (Slowloris) exhaustion.

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.text:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: pacto-dashboard
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: pacto-dashboard
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: pacto-dashboard
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: dashboard
          image: ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/dashboard:4.4.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
          env:
            - name: PACTO_DASHBOARD_REPO
              value: "ghcr.io/org/svc-a,ghcr.io/org/svc-b"
            - name: PACTO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: pacto-registry
                  key: token
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 3
            periodSeconds: 5
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 128Mi
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          volumeMounts:
            - name: cache
              mountPath: /home/pacto/.cache
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: cache
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: pacto-dashboard
spec:
  selector:
    app: pacto-dashboard
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 3000

docs.title: Pacto for Developers
docs.text:
You own the service, so you own its contract. This guide shows how to write one next to your code: a pacto.yaml file that says what your service exposes, what it needs and how it behaves. Platform engineers, CI and other teams then read the same file instead of asking you.

New to Pacto? Start with the five-minute Quickstart. The CLI reference lists every command and contract sections lists every field.

docs.title: Your workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Write code] --> B[Infer schemas]
    B --> C[Define pacto.yaml]
    C --> D[pacto validate]
    D --> F[pacto push]
    F --> G[CI / Platform picks it up]

docs.title: 1. Initialize your contract
docs.text:
pacto init my-service

This creates a my-service/ directory (a bundle) with a valid starter contract. Edit pacto.yaml to match your service.

docs.title: 2. Infer schemas from your code (optional)
docs.text: If your config already ships a JSON Schema, such as your Helm chart's values.schema.json, vendor that file into your bundle and point configurations[].schema at it. Otherwise the schema-infer plugin generates one from a config file.

docs.title: Generating a configuration schema
docs.text:
Pacto resolves the --option file= path relative to the bundle directory, so keep the config file inside the bundle. With config.yaml in my-service/:

pacto generate schema-infer my-service --option file=config.yaml -o my-service

This generates my-service/config.schema.json. Reference it in your contract:

configurations:
  - name: default
    required: true
    schema: config.schema.json

Secret leak trap

The plugin leaves your config.yaml sitting in the bundle, and a bundle directory is published whole. pacto pack and pacto push upload every file under it, so pacto pull hands your config values, secrets included, to anyone who can read the artifact. The contract needs only the inferred schema. Delete the input once the schema exists, or list it in .pactoignore if you want to keep it beside the contract.

docs.title: Generating an OpenAPI spec
docs.text:
If your service exposes an HTTP API using FastAPI or Huma, use the openapi-infer plugin to extract an OpenAPI 3.1 spec from your source code:

# Auto-detect the framework: FastAPI or Huma (generates interfaces/openapi.yaml)
pacto generate openapi-infer my-service -o my-service

# Override framework detection
pacto generate openapi-infer my-service -o my-service --option framework=fastapi

Both plugins need the pacto.yaml that step 1 wrote. The starter contract already points its api interface at interfaces/openapi.yaml. A contract that pacto init read from a Dockerfile and manifests has an interface only when it found an OpenAPI file, so add the interfaces entry yourself.

Both plugins live in a separate repository and ship as separate binaries. The installer script fetches them alongside the CLI; go install and make build build only pacto. See Official plugins for how to get them.

docs.title: 3. Define the contract
docs.text: See Contract sections for interfaces, workload, state and capabilities; Dependencies and state for dependencies; and Configuration and policy for configurations and policies.

docs.title: 4. Validate and push
docs.text:
pacto validate my-service
pacto push oci://ghcr.io/your-org/my-service-pacto -p my-service

See Validation layers for the rules and error codes. push validates before uploading; use --force to overwrite an existing tag. pacto push uploads only the contract, for use without delivery. For anything delivery should ship, use pacto publish, which signs the version and never overwrites one.

On Kubernetes, the operator checks what your service does on the network against this contract. See runtime conformance.

docs.text:
• Contract reference: every field, precisely
  • Composition patterns: the compositions these primitives are usually assembled into
  • CLI reference: every command and flag
  • For platform engineers: the other side of the same contract

docs.title: External evidence
docs.text:
Some environments cannot be watched from your platform: edge sites, air-gapped estates, customer tenants and short-lived CI runners. The external evidence protocol lets them report on themselves. The remote side signs a report and pushes it to you, and Pacto checks it against the contract.

Evidence is what a tool saw in a running system. Pacto carries it in an EvidenceSet: a list of observations about one service. In Kubernetes the operator gathers evidence itself, and the optional node agent adds what the kernel saw on the network (see runtime conformance). This page covers evidence that arrives from outside.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
The producer (the remote environment) makes a key, signs a report and sends it. The platform runs the receiving server.

# Producer: create a signing key bound to the producer "edge-eu-west".
pacto evidence keygen --producer edge-eu-west --key-id edge-eu-west-2026

# Producer: sign an EvidenceSet and send it.
pacto evidence sign evidence.json --key edge-eu-west-2026.key \
  --key-id edge-eu-west-2026 --producer edge-eu-west --sequence 1 > envelope.json
pacto evidence send envelope.json --url https://pacto.example.com/api/evidence/v1/envelopes

# Platform: accept reports about one exact contract revision.
pacto evidence serve --trust ./trust \
  --subject oci://registry.example.com/acme/payments-api@sha256:<digest>

Hand the edge-eu-west__edge-eu-west-2026.pub file to the platform and put it in ./trust.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Traffic goes one way. Pacto never connects to a remote environment; the remote side starts every request and only pushes. Accepted evidence is stored in your contract registry as an OCI 1.1 referrer: an artifact attached to the contract revision it is about. The registry is the only store, so the Evidence Server needs no bucket, volume or database.

GHCR cannot host Pacto evidence

GitHub Container Registry does not serve the native OCI Referrers API, which the Evidence Server requires. GHCR works for contracts; only evidence needs the Referrers endpoint. Publish contracts you want to carry evidence to a conformant registry (zot, Docker Hub, Harbor, ECR, ACR, Artifactory).

The protocol signs evidence envelopes: the wrapper around one report. Every envelope is Ed25519-signed and checked against a trust store (the list of public keys you accept) before it is stored.

docs.title: Wire format
docs.text:
An envelope carries exactly one EvidenceSet plus the identity, ordering and freshness metadata the platform needs to trust and place it.

Field Type Meaning apiVersion string Protocol version. Must be pacto.dev/evidence/v1. kind string Must be EvidenceEnvelope. id string Unique envelope id. The CLI defaults it to a sha256: hash over apiVersion, producer.id, sequence and the evidence, so two producers reporting identical evidence get different ids. producer.id string The environment that produced the envelope. Becomes the target's scope. producer.version string Optional producer or collector version. producer.keyId string Trust-store key id that signed this envelope. sequence uint64 Monotonic per-producer counter for replay and ordering. issuedAt RFC3339 When the envelope was signed. expiresAt RFC3339 End of the validity window. Zero disables expiry. evidenceSet object The Pacto EvidenceSet being reported. Top-level keys: Subject, ContractRef, Source, ObservedAt, Observations. signature object { "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "<base64>" } over the canonical bytes.

A full envelope on the wire:

{
  "apiVersion": "pacto.dev/evidence/v1",
  "kind": "EvidenceEnvelope",
  "id": "sha256:8f3c…",
  "producer": { "id": "edge-eu-west", "version": "1.4.2", "keyId": "edge-eu-west-2026" },
  "sequence": 42,
  "issuedAt": "2026-07-29T10:00:00Z",
  "expiresAt": "2026-07-30T10:00:00Z",
  "evidenceSet": {
    "Subject": { "kind": "service", "name": "payments-api" },
    "ContractRef": "oci://registry.example.com/acme/payments-api@sha256:1a2b…",
    "Source": "edge-collector",
    "ObservedAt": "2026-07-29T09:59:00Z",
    "Observations": [ … ]
  },
  "signature": { "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "2Q6d…gyZhDw==" }
}

Canonical bytes. The signature covers envelope JSON with the signature field omitted, re-encoded so map keys are sorted and whitespace is normalized. Transport formatting has no effect on verification.

Immutable contract references. A reported ContractRef must be an immutable oci://…@sha256:… digest reference. Local paths, bare refs and mutable tags are rejected.

Bounds. An envelope is capped at 1 MiB and may carry at most 10,000 observations. Oversized payloads are refused before parsing. Decoding rejects unknown fields and requires apiVersion, kind, id, producer.id and producer.keyId.

Complete observation payloads. An Observed observation must carry every verdict-bearing key for its kind, even when false: present (capability), type (workload), type and present (interface), reachable (dependency), durable (persistence) and present (configuration, plus conformant when present is true). Pacto rejects a missing or null key, so a gap never reads as a confirmed negative. Other keys, such as protocol, are optional.

Freshness and replay. issuedAt and expiresAt bound the validity window. Verification rejects expired or not-yet-valid envelopes. A zero expiresAt disables the expiry check. Each producer stamps a strictly increasing sequence. Ingestion rejects a repeated id or a non-increasing sequence. Replay protection runs inside the serialized commit, over a duplicate-id set and a per-producer sequence maximum. Both are re-derived from the registry on every commit, so they survive process restarts.

docs.title: Producers that ship with Pacto
docs.text:
Two Pacto commands observe a running service and send signed envelopes with the same --evidence-url, --evidence-key, --evidence-key-id and --evidence-producer flags, so you can use the protocol without building an EvidenceSet yourself:

  • pacto agent --sink evidence watches every bound workload on a host and sends one envelope per workload each round.
  • pacto run --evidence-url ... sends one envelope per round about the command it wraps.

Both sign with a 24-hour expiry and sequences that start at the wall clock in nanoseconds, so they keep increasing across restarts. Both need the contract pinned as oci://...@sha256:<digest>, which must also be one of the server's --subject values.

docs.title: CLI commands
docs.text: Command Side Purpose pacto evidence keygen producer Mint an Ed25519 signing keypair. Writes <keyId>.key (secret, 0600) and the public key. --producer is optional: with it the public key is <producer>__<keyId>.pub, binding the key to that producer; without it, a bare <keyId>.pub binds it to a producer named after the key id. pacto evidence sign producer Wrap an EvidenceSet in a signed envelope. Reads the EvidenceSet JSON, validates it, wraps it and signs with --key, --key-id, --producer, --sequence. Default --ttl 24h; --ttl 0 disables expiry. pacto evidence send producer Report a signed envelope outbound to an ingestion endpoint. POSTs to POST /api/evidence/v1/envelopes. pacto evidence verify either Verify a signed envelope against a trust store. Checks signature, freshness, producer authorization and trust. Exits non-zero on failure. pacto evidence serve platform Run the ingestion endpoint. Loads trust store from --trust, resolves every --subject (at least one required), verifies and evaluates envelopes and publishes results to the registry as OCI 1.1 referrers. Listens on 127.0.0.1:8686 or --listen-address.

docs.title: Ingestion HTTP API
docs.text:
The ingestion host mounts five endpoints under /api/evidence/v1.

Method + path Purpose Success POST /api/evidence/v1/envelopes Accept, verify, de-duplicate, evaluate and store one envelope. 202 Accepted with { id, compliance, findings, acceptedAt } GET /api/evidence/v1/health Liveness. Independent of the registry. 200 OK with { "status": "ok" } GET /api/evidence/v1/ready Readiness. 503 until every configured subject resolves and answers native Referrers discovery. 200 OK with { "status": "ready" } GET /api/evidence/v1/producers List the trusted producer ids the host advertises. 200 OK with { "producers": [ … ] } GET /api/evidence/v1/targets The latest accepted report per target for a read-only HTTP evidence source. 200 OK with the versioned targets DTO (schema pacto.dev/evidence-source/v2)

POST status codes. A non-2xx response is a JSON object { "code": <stable-code>, "message": <generic> }. The code is stable and the message is generic; neither contains the underlying error text, keys or signature bytes. The server logs verification failures and server-side errors and keeps them from the caller. TLS termination is the host's responsibility. Signature verification is always on and cannot be disabled.

Status Code When 202 Accepted — Verified, evaluated and stored. 400 Bad Request invalid_envelope The body could not be read or the envelope could not be decoded. 401 Unauthorized unauthorized_producer Signature, trust, freshness failure or the key is not authorized for this producer or subject. 409 Conflict replay A duplicate id or an out-of-sequence sequence. 422 Unprocessable Entity contract_ref_rejected The contract ref is not an approved immutable digest reference. 422 Unprocessable Entity invalid_evidence The EvidenceSet is invalid. 502 Bad Gateway contract_resolution_failed The referenced contract could not be resolved. 503 Service Unavailable store_not_ready The server has not yet resolved and enumerated its configured subjects. 503 Service Unavailable registry_unavailable, registry_incomplete The accepted history could not be read or could not be read completely, so the replay check could not run. 503 Service Unavailable store_degraded The record could not be published to the registry. 500 Internal Server Error internal_error An unexpected failure.

docs.title: Registry conformance
docs.text:
Native Referrers API is mandatory. Verify before configuring:

oras discover --distribution-spec v1.1-referrers-api <repo>@sha256:<digest>

A conformant registry answers GET /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest> with HTTP 200 and an OCI image index. A non-conformant one answers 404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN.

Registry Referrers API zot, Docker Hub, Harbor, ECR, ACR, Artifactory Yes GHCR, CNCF distribution (registry:2, registry:3) No Operation Requirement Permissions Pull (resolve contract, enumerate referrers, read payloads) and push (publish accepted record) on every configured subject's repository. Never deletes, never writes tags, never touches unconfigured repositories. Authentication Pacto OCI credential policy: explicit credential, pacto login, GITHUB_TOKEN for GHCR or Docker config. In Kubernetes: evidence.registry.credentialsSecret names an existing kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret. Subjects Explicit allow-list of exact immutable contract revisions: --subject oci://registry.example.com/acme/checkout@sha256:<64 hex>. Mutable tags, local paths, non-oci:// refs and catalog-wide discovery rejected. At least one required. Artifact format One untagged OCI manifest per accepted report. subject: contract digest from ContractRef. artifactType: application/vnd.pacto.evidence.record.v1+json. One layer carrying pacto.dev/evidence-record/v1. Deterministic build. Writer concurrency Single active writer: one replica, Recreate rollout strategy. Registry offers no compare-and-set. Commit: verify, mutex, enumerate all referrers, rebuild replay state, check replay globally, publish, confirm discoverable, return 202. State re-derived from registry. Retention and GC Pacto never deletes evidence. Retention, backup and GC are registry responsibilities. Exclude referrers of contract manifests from GC policies that prune untagged manifests. Deleting a subject deletes its evidence.

Registry write access is evidence write access. The signature is checked once at ingestion; the read path does not re-verify it.

Readiness and partial state. Writes fail closed when reads are incomplete.

State Meaning /ready /targets ready Every subject resolved, every referrer valid. 200 200, authoritative partial (bad artifact) Every subject resolved, some referrer unreadable. 200 200 with health.status: partial partial (bad subject) Some subject failed, others read. 503 200 with health.status: partial unavailable No subject readable. 503 503 registry_unavailable

Beside status, the health block carries the counts that say which half of a partial you have: subjects, failedSubjects and invalidArtifacts.

docs.title: Trust store and trust config
docs.text:
A trust store is a single .pub file or a directory of .pub files (base64 Ed25519 public keys). The filename binds the producer: <producerId>__<keyId>.pub authorizes key keyId for producer producerId, while a bare <keyId>.pub authorizes it for the producer whose id equals the key id.

Authentication and authorization are separate. An envelope whose keyId is not in the trust store is rejected as an unknown key. An unsigned envelope, an unsupported algorithm or a bad signature is rejected. After the signature checks out, the envelope's producer.id must match the key's bound producer, or it is rejected, so a trusted key cannot sign as another producer.

Rotation. Add a new <producerId>__<newKeyId>.pub, sign with the new keyId and remove the old entry. The producer identity survives the key change.

Structured trust configuration for per-key subject and contract-repository allowlists:

apiVersion: pacto.dev/evidence-trust/v1
keys:
  - keyId: edge-eu-west-2026
    producerId: edge-eu-west
    publicKeyFile: edge-eu-west__edge-eu-west-2026.pub
    allowedSubjects: [payments-*]                  # path.Match globs; empty = any
    allowedContractRepos: [registry.example.com/acme/contracts]  # prefixes; empty = any

Loading validates the schema version, identifier grammar, duplicate key ids, contradictory producer bindings, missing or traversing key files and malformed patterns.

Distributing the trust store is an out-of-band operator responsibility. The protocol verifies against whatever keys the host trusts and never fetches them. In Kubernetes the trust store is a Secret mounted read-only (evidence.trust.existingSecret).

For Kubernetes deployment (trust store creation, subject configuration, registry credentials), see The Evidence Server.

docs.text:
• Operational graph: where ingested targets appear and how freshness and completeness work
  • Collectors and the evidence boundary: how an EvidenceSet is produced and evaluated
  • CLI reference: the full command surface

docs.title: Fleet views
docs.text: Three ways to see all your services at once: the dashboard in a browser, pacto fleet in a terminal or CI job and pacto tui in an interactive terminal. All three read the same operational graph, the joined view of your contracts, their versions and where they run. An AI agent asks the same questions through the pacto_fleet_* tools of pacto mcp --fleet. The contract-to-infrastructure side is in For platform engineers.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
pacto dashboard opens a web dashboard over the same contracts the CLI manages and the operator checks. It has four views: what needs attention now, the service list, the Operational Graph and change analysis. It finds its sources at startup and merges them per service. Next to the Kubernetes operator it needs no OCI arguments: it reads the registry addresses from the resolvedRef field in each Pacto resource's status, then shows version history, interfaces, configuration schemas and diffs. See the pacto dashboard reference for its flags and environment variables.

Its HTTP API is described at /openapi.json; see Dashboard container.

docs.title: Fleet queries without a browser
docs.text:
pacto fleet answers the same questions from a terminal or a CI job: it builds one snapshot from the sources you name, then queries it with search, get, graph, status and explain.

$ pacto fleet search --local ./contracts --oci ghcr.io/acme/unreachable-pacto:1.0.0
1 of 1 service(s):
  payments-api                 NotEvaluated owner=acme/payments  revs=1 targets=0
warning: answer is partial (as of 2026-08-23T01:30:40+02:00)
  - [SOURCE_PARTIAL] source oci returned a partial result
  - [SOURCE_RECORD_INVALID] ref ghcr.io/acme/unreachable-pacto:1.0.0 could not be resolved: artifact not found: ghcr.io/acme/unreachable-pacto:1.0.0

Read the completeness before you read the rows. Pacto reports an unreachable registry, so a service missing from a partial answer may be one the missing source knew about. Likewise 1 of 1 is this page of total matches. --output-format json carries the same facts in a meta envelope for a CI job to branch on, and query semantics has the five operations and the knowledge vocabulary behind completeness.

docs.title: The terminal UI
docs.text:
pacto tui is the dashboard's terminal equivalent, built over the snapshot pacto fleet builds and taking the same source flags. It loads that snapshot once and opens on the Services tab. From there you move through services, revisions, targets, owners and sources, with whatever row is highlighted standing in as the argument, so you never type a path. It needs an interactive terminal; in a pipeline, use the plain commands.

One difference from the dashboard matters more than the rest: the dashboard only reads and the TUI also writes. Read verbs run in-process against the loaded snapshot. Write verbs shell out to this same binary so they own the terminal. Each one names what it is about to change before it waits for a y: the directory a pull will overwrite, the resolved plugin binary, the output directory a generate will write. Pass --read-only to remove the four write verbs from the in-TUI help screen.

# whatever bundles are under the current directory
pacto tui

# a populated screen from the committed demo fixture
pacto tui --local examples/demo/bundles \
  --target-state examples/demo/fleet-targets.yaml \
  --traces examples/demo/traces.json --freshness 24h

# the same demo with no clone at all, straight out of the registry
pacto tui --root oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/pacto-demo:1.0.0 --local ""

The second command needs a clone and a paste from the repository root; it opens on 36 services and 4 operational targets. The third needs nothing on disk: --root follows the published contract's dependency declarations and pulls 12 of the demo's 36 services out of ghcr.io, and --local "" switches off the default directory scan. A registry has no record of where anything runs, so every service reads NotEvaluated until you add the --target-state fixture.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Action tab / shift+tab cycle the tabs: kinds on the list, categories under a, direction on a graph / filter; enter applies it, esc discards what you typed enter open the highlighted row a what needs attention + / - graph depth ? toggle the key table for the current screen r reload the snapshot q back, or quit from the root screen esc clear an applied filter, otherwise the same as q y copy the equivalent pacto command v validate the selected bundle E / e explain the bundle, or explain it from the fleet's point of view l check the lock file d / i diff or impact between two selections, pressed twice g the selection's neighborhood graph p / P push, or pull (writes; asks first) L rewrite the lock file (writes; asks first) G run a generate plugin (writes; asks first)

y copies the command you would have typed to the clipboard, so you can run anything the TUI has no key for. The line is shell-quoted, so a value carrying a space or a semicolon still pastes as one argument. With no clipboard, for example over ssh or on a headless box, the TUI prints the line and the reason it could not copy it. See the pacto tui reference for every flag.

docs.title: GitHub Actions Integration
docs.text: The official Pacto CLI GitHub Action runs Pacto in your workflows: validate a contract, fail a pull request on a breaking change and publish the contract on release.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
The action is command-driven. command: setup installs the pacto binary. Every other command (validate, diff, push and doc) runs the pacto that an earlier command: setup step in the same job installed, and so do your own run: steps.

name: Contract CI

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'pacto.yaml'
      - 'interfaces/**'
      - 'configuration/**'
      - 'policy/**'

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Pacto CLI
        uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions@v1
        with:
          command: setup

      - name: Validate contract
        run: pacto validate .

docs.title: Detect breaking changes
docs.text:
pacto diff takes the old contract first and the new one second, and exits non-zero on a BREAKING result (see change classification rules):

      - name: Check for breaking changes
        uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions@v1
        with:
          command: diff
          old: oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto
          new: .
          comment-on-pr: 'true'

This step follows the setup step from the Quick start job. fail-on-breaking defaults to true, so a breaking change fails the step. comment-on-pr posts the diff on the pull request. It posts with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN, which is read-only by default: grant the job pull-requests: write, or the comment fails with a 403 even when the diff passes.

The action passes its github-token input, the workflow's token by default, to every command as GH_TOKEN. Pacto logs in to ghcr.io with that token through the gh CLI, which GitHub-hosted runners include, so a baseline on GHCR needs only permissions: packages: read. For any other registry, set PACTO_REGISTRY_USERNAME and PACTO_REGISTRY_PASSWORD on the step.

docs.title: Find who a change breaks
docs.text: The action has no impact command. Run pacto impact in a run: step after command: setup, as Put it in your repository shows.

docs.title: Publish on release
docs.text:
Push the contract bundle to an OCI registry when a release is created:

name: Publish Contract

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

jobs:
  push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Pacto CLI
        uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions@v1
        with:
          command: setup

      - name: Push contract
        uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions@v1
        with:
          command: push
          ref: oci://ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}-pacto
          path: .
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

docs.title: Action reference
docs.text: Every input is documented in the pacto-actions repository, which owns the action and its version history.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Give the step an id to read its outputs.

Output Set by Value version setup The exact Pacto version installed has-breaking-changes diff "true" or "false" diff-output diff The full diff output, in output-format doc-output doc The generated markdown documentation

has-breaking-changes is set from the CLI exit code. pacto diff exits non-zero on a BREAKING classification, so a POTENTIAL_BREAKING result reads "false". A diff that fails to run, for example on an unresolvable reference or an unparseable contract, also exits non-zero and so also reads "true"; check the step log before treating it as a contract verdict. The output is written whether or not fail-on-breaking stops the step, so you can gate on it yourself:

      - name: Check for breaking changes
        id: contract-diff
        uses: TrianaLab/pacto-actions@v1
        with:
          command: diff
          old: oci://ghcr.io/acme/my-service-pacto
          new: .
          fail-on-breaking: 'false'

      - name: Require an approved exception
        if: steps.contract-diff.outputs.has-breaking-changes == 'true'
        run: exit 1

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
This page defines every word these docs use with a special meaning, in alphabetical order. Each word is defined here once, and the link after it leads to the page that explains it in full. Other pages link here instead of explaining the word again. The dashboard and the command line use the same words. Where the dashboard shows a different label, the last column gives it.

Word Meaning In the dashboard Accept the unknown A person lets a change with an Unknown check go ahead. It is recorded as accepted, never as a pass. See What Unknown means Accept the unknown Admission policies Rules the Kubernetes cluster runs on every request before it accepts it. Pacto's check who may ask for and approve a change, and records say whether they were on (guarded). See Install — Agent An AI agent, such as Claude, that calls Pacto's tools over MCP. It can plan and ask for changes, and only a person approves one. See Who may approve. An agent you build is a service like any other: see an agent is a service. The pacto agent command is the runtime watcher; see Node agent Agent Anchor One fixed digest per Stage in the streams repository. Every record of that Stage hangs on it as a referrer, so the anchor is where the Stage's whole history is read. See Where records live — Approval A person's answer on one held change: approve, accept the unknown or reject. See Look, then decide Approve Argo CD A GitOps tool that applies Kubernetes files to a cluster. Pacto works with an OCI-sourced Argo CD Application, one that reads its files from an artifact in a registry, and moves a version by writing its digest onto it. See Apply through Argo CD — Auto-hold Set when someone rolls a Stage back by hand, or promotes it back to a version it already verified. Automation stops promoting there until a person unfreezes it or promotes a version it has not verified yet. See Roll back by hand — Break-glass A group, pacto:break-glass by default, allowed to force a version past every check. A forced version freezes the Stage. See Force a version — Breaking change A change that removes or changes something consumers may use. Pacto classifies every change as breaking, possibly breaking or non-breaking. See Change classification — Bundle A contract together with the files it points to (OpenAPI documents, schemas), as one folder or one published artifact.
