Position Where Who reads it Widening Narrowing request OpenAPI request bodies and parameters, MCP inputSchema the new provider, from an old caller NON_BREAKING BREAKING response OpenAPI responses, MCP outputSchema an old consumer, which may switch over every enum value BREAKING NON_BREAKING record AsyncAPI message payload and headers schemas old and new code at once, in both directions BREAKING BREAKING Edit Effect enum value added, oneOf or anyOf variant added or type member added widens type changed from integer to number, or nullable: true set widens maxLength, maximum, maxItems or maxProperties raised, or a min* bound lowered widens a bound, pattern, format, const, enum, allOf or items removed widens additionalProperties: false relaxed to a schema or removed widens required entry or the whole required list removed, or allOf member removed widens the mirror of each row above narrows enum or required entries reordered no change pattern, format, const or multipleOf rewritten, or type changed to an unrelated type breaks in every position anything inside not or if, a default, readOnly or discriminator changed, any other keyword breaks in every position a $ref Pacto cannot resolve POTENTIAL_BREAKING in every position an x- extension keyword added, removed or changed POTENTIAL_BREAKING in every position description, title, summary, example, examples, $comment, externalDocs, deprecated or tags NON_BREAKING in every position

Properties have their own rules:

  • Adding an optional property is NON_BREAKING in every position, because a reader tolerates a field it does not know.
  • Removing an optional property is BREAKING from a response or a record whether or not required listed it. Most payload schemas list nothing, and the field is data a reader may use.
  • Removing one from a request is POTENTIAL_BREAKING: the provider drops the caller's field unread.
  • An object with additionalProperties: false accepts no undeclared field, so adding a property widens it and removing one narrows it.
  • Inside a response's headers map every grade stops at POTENTIAL_BREAKING, because removing the whole header is POTENTIAL_BREAKING.

docs.title: References and components
docs.text:
Each $ref is resolved first, so a component is judged where it is used:

  • A component used in more than one position, such as a schema in a request body and in a response, is judged in each one. Pacto reports one change with the worst grade, at the usage path where that grade applies. The reason names the component and its usages.
  • Pacto compares what a ref resolves to. Renaming a component with identical content is no change, and a ref pointed at a different schema is graded by the structural difference.
  • Local refs (#/components/..., #/definitions/..., #/$defs/...) and relative file refs inside the bundle resolve, and a ref inside another file resolves against that file. Request bodies, responses, parameters and headers resolve the same way as schemas.
  • A remote (http or https) ref, or one whose target is missing, is POTENTIAL_BREAKING, and the reason says Pacto could not resolve it. The same unresolved ref in both revisions reports no change, because Pacto sees nothing change. A ref whose text stays the same while its target goes away, such as a renamed component or a file dropped from the bundle, is POTENTIAL_BREAKING at the usage path.
  • A ref to another ref resolves through the chain. A chain that loops never resolves.
  • A path item written as a $ref, local or to a file, is followed to the operations it holds.
  • A recursive schema is compared once per position, so cycles terminate.
  • A component that no path, channel or operation reaches through a $ref is reported as one NON_BREAKING change, because no consumer reads it. Security schemes are named without a $ref, so that report leaves them out.
  • In AsyncAPI 3 a ref from an operation to its channel or message is compared as text, because the channel is compared on its own.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
Field Change Classification readiness Added / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.expires Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.minScore Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.partialCredit Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING readiness.claims[] Added / Modified / Removed NON_BREAKING

All readiness changes are NON_BREAKING, because readiness tracks operational maturity and leaves runtime compatibility unchanged. Adding or removing the whole readiness block surfaces as a single readiness change; otherwise the gate fields (expires, minScore, partialCredit) are compared individually. Claims are keyed by id, and a claim whose status, weight, evidence or any other field changed is reported as a modification of that claim (for example readiness.claims[dashboard]). The diff skips the readiness.history revision log, an append-only changelog that changes on every release.

docs.title: Fields the diff skips
docs.text:
Section Behavior metadata Skipped. Free-form metadata keys appear in documentation and the dashboard. capabilities[].binding Skipped. Capabilities are keyed by type (and ref), so pacto diff reports no change for a new binding.interface or binding.path on an otherwise unchanged capability. readiness.history[] Skipped. An append-only changelog that changes on every release; see Readiness.

To flag changes to these fields in CI, gate on them separately, for example with a policy or a custom check.

docs.title: SBOM
docs.text:
SBOM changes are reported separately from contract changes. They are informational and leave the overall diff classification unchanged.

Change Description Package added A new package appears in the SBOM Package removed A package left the SBOM Package version modified A package's version changed Package license modified A package's license changed Package supplier modified A package's supplier changed

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: environments lists the environments a service runs in and the configuration values each one uses. pacto validate checks those values against the schema of every configuration they name, on every change. Pacto applies nothing and deploys nothing. The other sections are in Contract sections and Configuration and policy.

docs.title: environments
docs.text:
Optional. Needs pactoVersion: "2.3": an older contract with it fails validation with NEEDS_PACTO_2_3. 2.3 needs Pacto core 4.4.0 or later and operator 6.4.0 or later; see Versions.

pactoVersion: "2.3"
service:
  name: web
  version: 1.4.0
configurations:
  - name: app
    schema: configuration/schema.json
    required: true
    values:
      LOG_LEVEL: info
  - name: chart
    schema: chart/values.schema.json
    required: true
environments:
  - name: staging
    file: environments/staging.yaml
  - name: production
    file: environments/production.yaml
Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, at most 63 characters. Unique in the contract (DUPLICATE_ENVIRONMENT_NAME otherwise) file string Yes Path to a YAML or JSON file, from the bundle root, with no leading / or ./ and no .. (FILE_NOT_FOUND otherwise, or when the file is missing)

The file maps each configuration name to the values that environment uses for it:

# environments/production.yaml
app:
  LOG_LEVEL: warn
chart:
  replicaCount: 5
  ingress:
    host: shop.example.com

The -f/--values and --set flags change the contract itself; an environment's values live in its file.

The file is part of the bundle, so pacto pack and pacto push ship it with the contract. A .pactoignore entry that hides it makes validation report FILE_NOT_FOUND.

docs.title: How values are checked
docs.text:
For each environment, and for each configuration its file names, Pacto merges the environment's values over the configuration's default values and checks the result against the configuration's schema. Objects merge key by key, and the environment's value wins. A null removes its key from the merged values, at any depth, so an environment can drop a default:

# environments/staging.yaml
chart:
  ingress:
    className: null  # staging uses the cluster's default ingress class

A configuration named with no values, such as app:, keeps its defaults. A required: true configuration that the file leaves out must pass its schema with its defaults alone. A configuration that is optional and left out is not checked.

Condition Code The file names a configuration the contract does not declare ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION The merged values fail the configuration's schema, or the file does not parse, is not a mapping of configuration names or has a key that is not a string ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID A required configuration has no values in the file and its defaults fail its schema ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_MISSING The configuration names its schema by ref, so the bundle holds no schema to check against, or there are no bundle files to read ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_UNVERIFIED (warning)

Each error names the environment, the configuration and the JSON Pointer of the value, and points at its line in the environment's file. A key that holds a dot or a slash, such as prometheus.io/scrape, is one step of the pointer, with / written as ~1 and ~ as ~0. The checks run in the environments stage of pacto validate.

Values hold references to secrets, such as a Secret or ExternalSecret name. Keep secret material out of the environment files, as you keep it out of the contract; see Secret references.

docs.title: Catch a chart change that breaks an environment
docs.text:
A Helm chart's values.schema.json is a JSON Schema, so you can reference it as a configuration and keep one file per environment. Version 1.4.0 of the web service ships this chart schema:

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "replicaCount": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
    "ingress": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"host": {"type": "string"}}
    }
  }
}

The contract references it and lists two environments:

pactoVersion: "2.3"
service:
  name: web
  version: 1.4.0
  owner: {team: storefront}
configurations:
  - name: chart
    schema: chart/values.schema.json
    required: true
environments:
  - name: staging
    file: environments/staging.yaml
  - name: production
    file: environments/production.yaml

Staging sets an ingress host. Production sets only a class name:

# environments/staging.yaml
chart:
  replicaCount: 1
  ingress:
    host: staging.example.com

# environments/production.yaml
chart:
  replicaCount: 5
  ingress:
    className: nginx

Version 1.5.0 updates the chart, and its schema makes ingress.host required. pacto validate reports the environment it breaks before you deploy it:

$ pacto validate web-1.5.0
web-1.5.0 is invalid
PASS load
SKIP lock         no pacto.lock
PASS structural
PASS cross-field
PASS policy
FAIL environments
  web-1.5.0/environments/production.yaml:3:3: ERROR [ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID] environments[1].file: environment production: configuration chart at /chart/ingress: missing property 'host'
SKIP guarantees   no dependency declares requires
SKIP readiness    not requested (--readiness)
SKIP closure      not requested (--closure)
Next: fix environments[1].file at web-1.5.0/environments/production.yaml:3:3 [ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID], then run pacto validate web-1.5.0
validation failed with 1 error(s)

The command exits 1. Add the host to the production file and run pacto validate again. pacto diff then lists the schema change and the new value:

$ pacto diff web-1.4.0 web-1.5.0
Classification: BREAKING
Required bump: major
Changes (4):
  [NON_BREAKING] service.version (modified): service.version modified [1.4.0 -> 1.5.0]
  [POTENTIAL_BREAKING] schema.properties.ingress.properties.className (added): schema.properties.ingress.properties.className added [+ map[type:string]]
  [BREAKING] schema.properties.ingress.required (added): schema.properties.ingress.required added [+ [host]]
  [NON_BREAKING] environments[production].chart.ingress.host (added): environments[production].chart.ingress.host added [+ shop.example.com]
breaking changes detected

docs.title: What a change needs
docs.text:
pacto diff compares environments by name:

Change Classification An environment added Non-breaking: it only adds values to check An environment removed Potentially breaking: the environment may still run the service A value in an environment's file added, removed or changed, at environments[<name>].<configuration>.<path> Non-breaking: the values are this service's own inputs, and only the service reads them

docs.title: Environments and Stages
docs.text:
When delivery promotes a version, it matches the Stage's spec.environment against the environment names the version's contract declares. The pacto.environment check runs the same environments stage as pacto validate, on the version's own bundle:

The version's contract The promote Declares no environments Goes on. The check says it does not apply Declares environments, but none named like the Stage's spec.environment Waits for the service's team to approve it Declares that environment, and its values fail with an error from the table above Waits for the service's team to approve it, with each error located in the file Declares that environment, and its values are ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_UNVERIFIED Waits for a person to accept the unknown Declares that environment, and its values pass Goes on

Name each environment after the spec.environment of the Stages that deliver the service there, such as staging and production.

docs.title: Contract overrides
docs.text:
Overrides change contract values at the command line without editing pacto.yaml, the same way Helm values work:

pacto validate . --set service.version=2.0.0 -f values-prod.yaml

Overrides are available on all commands that take a contract reference: validate, explain, doc, generate, graph, pack, push and lock. The two commands that take a pair of contracts (diff, impact) use the prefixed flags in Diff overrides. See the CLI reference for the complete command and flag listing.

docs.title: Override flags
docs.text:
Flag Short Description --values <file> -f Merge a YAML values file into the contract --set <key=value> Set an individual value using dot-notation

Note

On pacto push, -f is the shorthand for --force, so spell out --values.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Overrides follow the same precedence logic as Helm (lowest to highest):

  1. Base pacto.yaml
  2. Values files (-f), in the order they are specified
  3. --set values

Later sources override earlier ones. Multiple -f flags apply in order, and the last file wins for any conflicting key.

docs.title: --set type inference
docs.text:
--set key=value infers the value's type from the string, trying in order: integer (int64) → float (float64) → boolean → string. The first parse that succeeds wins, and a value that matches none stays a string. For example:

  • --set readiness.minScore=80 → integer 80; --set ratio=1.5 → float 1.5.
  • --set flag=true → boolean true (but --set flag=1 → integer 1).
  • A multi-dot semver like --set service.version=1.0.0 has two dots, so it matches none of the numeric or boolean types and stays a string. A two-segment value like 1.0 parses as the float 1.0. Set values that must stay strings in a -f values file with explicit YAML typing.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Override the service version
pacto validate my-service --set service.version=2.0.0

# Use a values file for environment-specific overrides
pacto validate my-service -f staging-values.yaml

# Combine both (--set takes precedence over -f)
pacto validate my-service -f staging-values.yaml --set service.version=3.0.0

# Set configuration values validated against the config schema
pacto validate my-service --set configurations[0].values.DB_HOST=localhost

# Set array elements using bracket notation
pacto validate my-service --set interfaces[0].visibility=internal

Configurations as composable claims shows a worked per-environment layout: one values file per environment, the array-replacement caveat and this precedence rule applied end to end.

docs.title: Diff overrides
docs.text:
diff and impact each take two contract references, an old one and a new one. To override each side independently, use these prefixed flags:

Flag Description --old-values <file> Values file for the old (first) contract --old-set <key=value> Set value for the old contract --new-values <file> Values file for the new (second) contract --new-set <key=value> Set value for the new contract 
# Override only the new contract
pacto diff oci://ghcr.io/acme/svc-pacto:1.0.0 my-service --new-set service.version=2.0.0

# Override both contracts
pacto diff old-service new-service \
  --old-values old-env.yaml \
  --new-values new-env.yaml \
  --new-set service.version=3.0.0

# The same four flags work on impact
pacto impact old-service new-service --new-set service.version=2.0.0

docs.title: Schema validation
docs.text:
Every command validates the contract against the Pacto JSON Schema after it applies overrides, so every command rejects invalid enum values, unknown fields and type mismatches.

# Rejected: "invalid" is not a valid enum value for state.type
pacto explain my-service --set state.type=invalid

# Rejected: "unknownField" is not defined in the schema
pacto doc my-service --set service.unknownField=value

docs.title: Publish
docs.text: publish says what a service publishes, where each artifact goes and how it is built. Only pacto publish reads it. The other sections are in Contract sections, Configuration and policy, Dependencies and state and Readiness.

docs.title: publish
docs.text:
Optional. Needs pactoVersion: "2.1": a 2.0 contract with a publish section fails validation with NEEDS_PACTO_2_1. Every other 2.0 contract keeps working unchanged. Pacto core older than 4.1.0 and operator older than 6.1.0 reject a 2.1 contract, and that includes your consumers. Once you publish a 2.1 bundle, a consumer on an older Pacto or operator fails to resolve it as a dependency. Have your consumers upgrade first.

pactoVersion: "2.1"
service: {name: payments, version: 2.4.0}  # every tag is this version
publish:
  bundle: oci://ghcr.io/acme/pacto/payments  # the contract bundle
  deploy: manifests                          # the artifact Flux applies
  artifacts:
    - name: api
      type: image
      ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/payments       # no tag
      build:
        command: [./hack/build-image.sh]     # an OCI layout to $PACTO_OUT, and the SBOM
      sbom: sbom/api.spdx.json               # sbom/ is listed in .pactoignore
    - name: manifests
      type: manifests
      ref: oci://ghcr.io/acme/deploy/payments
      build:
        command: [./hack/render.sh]          # writes a directory to $PACTO_OUT
  sign: {key: cosign.key}
Field Meaning bundle Required. The repository the contract bundle goes to, as oci://host/path with no tag deploy The name of the manifests artifact a Flux Kustomization applies. Pacto adds the delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/contract annotation to it and tags it last artifacts[].name Unique. Later builds see the digest as PACTO_DIGEST_<NAME> (upper case, - becomes _) artifacts[].type image, chart or manifests artifacts[].ref The repository, as oci://host/path with no tag artifacts[].build.dockerfile context, optional file and platforms. Runs docker buildx into an OCI image layout. Images only artifacts[].build.command A command run in the contract directory that writes the artifact to $PACTO_OUT: an OCI image layout for an image, one .tgz for a chart, files for manifests artifacts[].sbom The SPDX (.spdx.json) or CycloneDX (.cdx.json) JSON file the build writes, relative to the contract directory. Pacto attaches it to the image and signs it. The image's build command must write it, for example with syft dir:. -o spdx-json=sbom/api.spdx.json inside the command. Pacto refuses a file older than the build, and refuses sbom on a dockerfile build because that build writes no SBOM. A path inside the contract directory must be in .pactoignore (publish --plan names the line). Images only sign Exactly one of keyless: true, key (a PEM key file, such as a cosign key) or kms (a KMS key URI, which needs a pacto built with -tags kms). transparencyLog: false keeps signatures out of the public log (pacto init --no-transparency-log writes it); keyless signing refuses it. Publishing refuses without sign sign.identity, sign.issuer Required with keyless: true: the certificate identity the signature carries and its OIDC issuer. Pacto keeps or adopts only what this identity signed

Builders write to $PACTO_OUT and Pacto does all the pushing. It pushes every artifact to a new tag, signs each digest with Sigstore and stamps org.opencontainers.image.version and org.opencontainers.image.revision on each manifest it pushes. A chart can be published but cannot be the deploy artifact, because the promoter confirms a release only through Kustomizations.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text: readiness is a checklist a team fills in about its own service, such as "we have a runbook" or "we load-tested it". Pacto turns it into a score and flags it when the score is too low or the assessment has expired. The other sections are in Contract sections, Configuration and policy and Dependencies and state.

docs.title: readiness
docs.text:
Optional. A pactoVersion: "2.0" feature. Declares operational readiness state for the service in a provider-neutral way. Each claim has a completion status, optional category and weight. The assessment includes an expiry date and scoring configuration. Pacto computes a readiness score from claim statuses and weights.

Readiness is a declared self-assessment: it records what the service's authors say they have done. Pacto checks the arithmetic and the expiry. The underlying work stays the authors' claim. Compliance is a separate verdict, decided from observed evidence about a running workload. The dashboard shows readiness on a revision and as a Needs attention category, and keeps it out of compliance verdicts.

readiness:
  expires: "2027-06-30"  # assessment-level expiry (YYYY-MM-DD)
  minScore: 80           # gate: the derived score must be >= this (omitted ⇒ 100)
  partialCredit: 0.5     # weight multiplier for partial claims (omitted ⇒ 0.5)

  claims:
    - id: dashboard
      type: url
      status: done
      category: observability
      weight: 20
      evidence: https://grafana.example.com/d/service-dashboard
      description: Main production dashboard

    - id: runbook
      type: document
      status: partial
      category: documentation
      weight: 15
      evidence: docs/runbook.md
      description: Incident runbook exists but missing escalation procedures

    - id: security-review
      type: ticket
      status: not-done
      category: security
      weight: 25
      evidence: JIRA-1234
      description: Security assessment pending

    - id: legacy-cleanup
      type: ticket
      status: deferred
      category: code-quality
      weight: 10
      evidence: TECH-5678
      description: Post-launch cleanup task

  history:
    - date: "2026-12-15"
      version: 1.0.0
      author: alice
      description: Initial readiness assessment

readiness.expires, readiness.claims[] and per-claim status are required when readiness is present. readiness.minScore, readiness.partialCredit and readiness.history[] are optional.

readiness fields:

Field Type Required Constraints expires string Yes Assessment-level expiry as a strict YYYY-MM-DD date. If the current date is past this date, ALL claims earn 0 weight regardless of status. Parsing is exact round-trip: zero-padded fields required and the value must re-serialize unchanged, so 2026-1-1, RFC 3339 timestamps and impossible dates (for example 2026-02-30) are rejected. minScore integer No Gate threshold on the same 0–100 scale as the score. Omitted ⇒ 100 (every claim must be complete). Checked by pacto validate --readiness and the operator. partialCredit number No Multiplier for partial status claims (0.0–1.0). Omitted ⇒ 0.5 (half credit). claims Claim[] Yes At least one claim. history HistoryEntry[] No Audit trail of readiness assessment changes.

docs.title: Claim fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Constraints id string Yes Stable readiness requirement id. Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]*[a-z0-9])?$. Unique within the contract. Policies usually target this field. type string Yes Enum: url, document, ticket, report, artifact, identifier, other. Evidence type. status string Yes Enum: done, partial, not-done, deferred. Completion state for the claim. category string No Enum: architecture, testing, code-quality, observability, security, documentation, infrastructure, ci-cd, deployment, resilience, backup-recovery, incident-response, compliance, other. Categorizes the requirement type. weight integer Yes Contribution to the readiness score. Range 0–100. evidence string Yes Where the evidence lives: a URL, a bundle-relative file path, a ticket ID or any other string. Pacto checks only that it is non-empty. It never fetches the value, resolves a path or verifies that the target exists, so the evidence is your claim. interfaces[].ref and configurations[].schema, by contrast, must exist in the bundle. description string No Optional human-readable explanation (non-blank when present).

docs.title: History entry
docs.text:
Field Type Required Constraints date string Yes Date of the change as YYYY-MM-DD. version string Yes Contract version at the time of the change. Non-blank. author string Yes Person or system that made the change. Non-blank. description string Yes Description of what changed.

The service owner is declared at the contract level, so readiness claims carry no per-claim owner. Tooling computes the readiness score (pacto explain, the dashboard and the operator) from claim statuses, weights, the assessment expiry and the current time. The contract stores no score.

docs.title: Readiness score and gate
docs.text:
If assessment is expired (today > readiness.expires):
  score = 0

Otherwise:
  earnedWeight = sum of earned weights for all in-scope claims
    - deferred claims: excluded from both numerator and denominator
    - done: full weight
    - partial: round(weight × partialCredit)
    - not-done: 0

  totalWeight = sum of weights for all in-scope claims (excluding deferred)
  score = round(earnedWeight / totalWeight × 100)

passing = score >= minScore          # minScore defaults to 100

Worked example. Using the four claims from the example above (weights 20, 15, 25, 10):

  • legacy-cleanup has status: deferred → excluded from both numerator and denominator
  • In-scope weights: 20 + 15 + 25 = 60 (total)
  • dashboard (done, weight 20) → earns 20
  • runbook (partial, weight 15) → earns round(15 × 0.5) = 8
  • security-review (not-done, weight 25) → earns 0
  • Earned weight: 20 + 8 + 0 = 28
  • Score: round(28 / 60 × 100) = round(46.7) = 47

Weights are relative. The score normalizes by totalWeight, so only the ratio of weights matters. A weight of 20 reads as "20%" only when the weights sum to 100. Weights can sum to any value. When they sum to 100, each one reads as a percentage. pacto explain and the dashboard show each claim's normalized contribution.

The gate (minScore) is a readiness threshold. With minScore: 80 you require 80% weighted completion, and a lower score fails the gate. Tooling evaluates the gate separately from contract validity:

  • pacto explain shows Gate: PASS/FAIL (score N / minScore M).
  • pacto validate --readiness (off by default) fails when score < minScore. It is opt-in because it depends on the current time, which would make plain validate non-deterministic.
  • The operator sets status.readiness.passing and the ReadinessSatisfied condition from the same rule.

Because minScore is an authored literal, a policy can require it org-wide, for example readiness.minScore >= 80. Presence rules live in policies and the threshold lives here.

docs.title: Requiring claims with policies
docs.text:
The base schema requires no specific claim. You express organizational standards as policies using standard JSON Schema. For example, to require a dashboard claim with status: done, category: observability and weight >= 20:

{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["readiness"],
  "properties": {
    "readiness": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["claims"],
      "properties": {
        "claims": {
          "type": "array",
          "contains": {
            "type": "object",
            "required": ["id", "status", "category", "weight"],
            "properties": {
              "id": { "const": "dashboard" },
              "status": { "const": "done" },
              "category": { "const": "observability" },
              "weight": { "minimum": 20 }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Combine multiple contains under allOf to require several claims (for example dashboard, runbook and security-review). JSON Schema cannot express some constraints, such as "total weight must equal 100", and Pacto has no other policy engine for them yet.

docs.title: Contract sections
docs.text: The fields that name a service, say who owns it and list what it exposes: pactoVersion, service, interfaces, capabilities, metadata and extensions. Configuration and policy are in Configuration and policy; dependencies and state are in Dependencies and state; readiness is in Readiness.

docs.title: pactoVersion
docs.text:
The contract specification version: "2.0", "2.1", "2.2" or "2.3". 2.1 adds publish, checks, external dependencies and the mcp interface type. 2.2 adds the interface lifecycle, an interface's compatibilityEpoch, its guarantees and dependencies[].requires. 2.3 adds environments. Every 2.0 contract is also valid under 2.1, every 2.1 contract under 2.2 and every 2.2 contract under 2.3. A 2.1 contract needs Pacto core 4.1.0 or later and operator 6.1.0 or later. A 2.2 contract needs Pacto core 4.3.0 or later and operator 6.3.0 or later. A 2.3 contract needs Pacto core 4.4.0 or later and operator 6.4.0 or later; see Versions.

pactoVersion: "2.0"

The version picks the JSON Schema the contract is validated against: pacto-v2.0.schema.json, pacto-v2.1.schema.json, pacto-v2.2.schema.json or pacto-v2.3.schema.json. Any other value is a hard error: the contract fails to load before validation runs and reports PARSE_ERROR (unsupported pactoVersion "3.0"; supported: 2.0, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3). See Validation layers.

docs.title: service
docs.text:
Identifies the service.

Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$ version string Yes Parses as semver (for example 2.1.0). See the note below owner OwnerInfo No Object only (string form removed)

service carries identity only. The contract has no image or chart field: how you build and deploy a service is a delivery concern that lives outside the contract.

version is parsed leniently, so write it strictly

Pacto accepts any version that Masterminds/semver can parse. That parser fills in the parts you leave out and accepts a leading v, so 1, 0.1 and v0.1 all validate and all mean 0.1.0-style coerced versions. 1.2.3.4, abc, a capital V1.0.0 and anything with surrounding whitespace are rejected with INVALID_SEMVER.

Later steps keep the coerced string as written, so that string is what gets published. pacto push tags the artifact with the literal string, and two contracts written 1 and 1.0.0 become two different tags of the same version. Write the full MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and skip the v.

docs.title: OwnerInfo
docs.text:
Structured ownership metadata. All fields are optional but at least one must be present. The field you set decides the canonical owner key that the graph groups by. See Ownership and the canonical owner key.

Field Type Required Constraints team string No The team's bare name, such as billing: usually the team label on its workloads. pacto init and pacto_check flag a team/ prefix dri string No Directly Responsible Individual contacts OwnerContact[] No Contact points

docs.title: OwnerContact
docs.text:
Field Type Required Constraints type string Yes One of: email, url, group, oncall, chat, other value string Yes Non-empty purpose string No One of: ownership, support, escalation, oncall, notifications

Examples:

# Structured form (the owner is always an object)
service:
  owner:
    team: foundations
    dri: eduardo.diaz
    contacts:
      - type: email
        value: foundations@acme.com
        purpose: ownership
      - type: chat
        value: "#foundations"

# Minimal object form (at least one field required)
service:
  owner:
    team: payments

docs.title: interfaces
docs.text:
Declares the service's communication boundaries. Optional: a service with no network interfaces, such as a batch job or shared library, can omit this section. The ref field points at the spec you already publish: an OpenAPI document, an AsyncAPI document, a gRPC service descriptor or the MCP tools a service exposes. Pacto reads that spec in place.

Field Type Required Constraints name string Yes Non-empty. Must be unique across interfaces type string Yes Enum: openapi, asyncapi, grpc, mcp (2.1) ref string Yes Non-empty. Path to the spec file within the bundle visibility string No Enum: public, internal. Default: internal lifecycle object No 2.2. See interface lifecycle guarantees object No 2.2. Behavior consumers may rely on. See Guarantees compatibilityEpoch integer No 2.2. Minimum 0. Default: 0. See Compatibility epoch

docs.title: Interface types
docs.text:
Value Spec kind openapi OpenAPI document for HTTP/REST traffic asyncapi AsyncAPI document for event-driven communication grpc gRPC service descriptor mcp The tools a service such as an AI agent exposes, as an MCP tools/list result. See an agent is a service

Note

Interface names must be unique within a contract. Every interface requires a non-empty ref (SCHEMA_VIOLATION otherwise), and the referenced file must exist in the bundle (FILE_NOT_FOUND otherwise). A .json, .yaml or .yml ref must also parse (INVALID_INTERFACE_SPEC otherwise). For any other extension, such as a gRPC .proto, Pacto checks only that the file exists. Ports are a deployment concern, so interfaces have no port field. Declare health and metrics endpoints as capabilities.

docs.title: Interface lifecycle
docs.text:
A provider retires an interface on a schedule its consumers can see. A lifecycle marks the interface deprecated:

interfaces:
  - name: orders-v1
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/orders-v1.yaml
    lifecycle:
      deprecated: "2026-10-01"
      sunset: "2027-04-01"
      successor: orders-v2
  - name: orders-v2
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/orders-v2.yaml
Field Type Required Constraints deprecated string Yes YYYY-MM-DD. The date the interface was deprecated sunset string No YYYY-MM-DD, not before deprecated. The date from which the interface may be removed successor string No Another interface of this service, or an absolute URL such as an oci:// reference to another service

pacto validate --closure warns a consumer about each deprecated interface of the services it depends on; see Dependency closure. A dependency names a service and not an interface, so the consumer is warned about every deprecated interface of that service. pacto diff reports the schedule; see change classification.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
guarantees declares the behavior a consumer may rely on, in a closed vocabulary: an unknown key fails to load.

Guarantee Value For Stronger value delivery at-most-once or at-least-once events Neither: they trade loss for duplicates ordering per-key or global events global, which also orders every key dedupeWindow duration events Longer retention duration events Longer idempotent boolean calls true timeout duration calls Shorter profile "1" both The vocabulary version. Omitted means 1

A duration is written like 500ms, 5m or 168h.

interfaces:
  - name: order-events
    type: asyncapi
    ref: interfaces/events.yaml
    guarantees:
      delivery: at-least-once
      ordering: per-key
      dedupeWindow: 10m
      retention: 168h

A consumer lists what it relies on in dependencies[].requires. pacto diff classifies a removed or weakened guarantee as breaking.

docs.title: Compatibility epoch
docs.text:
Raise compatibilityEpoch when an interface's behavior changes incompatibly while its spec stays the same, for example when an amount field switches from cents to euros. pacto diff reports the change as BREAKING with the interface's name in the reason, so pacto impact lists the consumers to review.

interfaces:
  - name: payments-api
    type: openapi
    ref: interfaces/openapi.yaml
    compatibilityEpoch: 2

An epoch only goes up. Lowering it is also BREAKING, because consumers that adapted to the higher epoch break in turn. A "2.0" or "2.1" contract that sets it reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_2.

docs.title: Interfaces at runtime
docs.text:
The Kubernetes operator checks two fields of a running interface: type and visibility.

  • type. The operator sends a probe to the port and looks at the protocol that answers. openapi accepts HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 and grpc accepts HTTP/2. Anything else is INTERFACE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH. A TLS port, no answer and asyncapi stay unverified.
  • visibility (internal when omitted). It is contradicted only when the operator sees an address outside private networks: a public externalIPs entry, or a LoadBalancer Service (without an internal load balancer annotation) or an Ingress whose status carries a public IP or hostname. That is INTERFACE_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH. A NodePort Service, an internal or address-less load balancer and an HTTPRoute leave exposure unknown, so the field stays unverified. A public interface seen only in-cluster also stays unverified, because a gateway the operator cannot see may expose it.

A field the operator cannot check leaves the contract status unchanged. See Runtime conformance.

docs.title: capabilities
docs.text:
Optional. Declares standard observability capabilities (health, metrics) or custom extension capabilities. Use this section to tell the platform that a service exposes health and metrics endpoints.

Field Type Required Constraints type string Yes Enum: health, metrics, extension ref string Conditional Required for extension only. A namespaced identifier (e.g. example.com/custom). Not allowed for health/metrics binding Binding No Standard types only (health/metrics). Binds the endpoint to a declared interface. Not allowed for extension

docs.title: Capability binding
docs.text:
Binds a standard capability endpoint (health/metrics) to a declared interface so a collector can probe it. binding.type is a closed set and http is the only supported transport in this release. Any other transport fails structural validation.

A binding resolves as follows:

  • binding.type: http means the capability is probed over HTTP.
  • binding.interface names the declared interface that provides the address and port for the probe. It is the platform-neutral counterpart of the Kubernetes CR's spec.target.interfaceBindings[].interface, which resolves to a concrete Kubernetes Service port. The capability path is independent of that interface's OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or gRPC specification.
  • binding.path is relative to the resolved endpoint.
Field Type Required Constraints type string Yes Enum: http (only supported transport; any other value fails validation) interface string Yes Must match a declared interfaces[].name: the interface whose platform binding provides the address and port (CAPABILITY_INTERFACE_UNKNOWN otherwise) path string No Application path relative to the resolved endpoint. Must start with a single / and carry no scheme/host/fragment (CAPABILITY_PATH_INVALID otherwise) 
capabilities:
  - type: health
    binding:
      type: http
      interface: rest-api
      path: /health
  - type: metrics
    binding:
      type: http
      interface: rest-api
      path: /metrics
  - type: extension
    ref: example.com/tracing

You can declare a health or metrics capability with no binding. Another collector can verify that declaration. The Kubernetes integration reports an unbound capability as Unsupported/Unknown because it has no endpoint to probe. An extension capability requires a namespaced ref and cannot declare a binding. Pacto has no evaluator for extensions, so it lists each one in coverage.unverified as capabilities[ref=<ref>] and excludes it from required assertions. A contract that declares one can still reach Compliant, and that verdict covers none of its extensions.

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
Optional. Free-form key-value pairs for organizational use. Pacto validates only the type.

metadata:
  team: payments
  tier: critical
  on-call: "#payments-oncall"

The schema sets additionalProperties: false at every level except inside metadata, so an unknown field fails validation.

Tip

metadata is a deliberate extension point for tooling. Platform teams use it to attach signals that their CI or deployment systems read from a contract. For example, infrastructure contracts can carry metadata.labels like platform/provisioner: crossplane to drive provisioning generically. See Infrastructure contracts.

docs.title: extensions
docs.text:
Optional. A free-form object for forward-compatible, namespaced extension data outside the core contract model. Use metadata for organizational key-value pairs and extensions for structured data that future Pacto features or third-party tools interpret. Namespace each key, for example with a domain, to avoid collisions. In this release Pacto validates only the type.

extensions:
  example.com/custom-tool:
    enabled: true

docs.title: Validation layers
docs.text:
pacto validate tells you whether a contract is well-formed before anyone relies on it. Run it in the bundle directory:

pacto validate .

It runs three checks in order and then the environments stage, and so does anything else that has to trust a contract. pack, push and publish refuse before they write or transmit a byte, and the operator revalidates every bundle it loads. Each layer short-circuits: if it fails, the layers after it are skipped, so one broken field can hide the rest.

docs.title: Layer 1: Structural (JSON Schema)
docs.text:
Validates against the embedded schema of the contract's version, pacto-v2.0.schema.json, pacto-v2.1.schema.json, pacto-v2.2.schema.json or pacto-v2.3.schema.json:

  • Field types match
  • Required fields are present (including the mandatory required on configurations[] and dependencies[])
  • Enum values are valid (for example interface type is openapi/asyncapi/grpc/mcp, capabilities[].type is health/metrics/extension, policies[].target is contract)
  • Fields that must carry a value are non-empty (for example interfaces[].ref and checks[].file)
  • Discriminated shapes hold: a configurations[] entry has exactly one of schema or ref, a capabilities[] extension requires a namespaced ref and health or metrics sets no ref
  • State invariants hold (stateless requires ephemeral durability)

Structural failures report SCHEMA_VIOLATION. A "2.0" contract that uses publish, checks, an external dependency or an mcp interface reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_1 for each instead: set pactoVersion: "2.1", which keeps every 2.0 field. A "2.0" or "2.1" contract that uses an interface lifecycle, compatibilityEpoch or guarantees or a dependency requires reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_2 for each: set pactoVersion: "2.2". A "2.0", "2.1" or "2.2" contract that declares environments reports NEEDS_PACTO_2_3: set pactoVersion: "2.3".

A contract that fails to load, because of malformed YAML, an unknown field or a pactoVersion other than "2.0", "2.1", "2.2" or "2.3", fails before any layer runs and reports PARSE_ERROR. Loading is the parse step that turns pacto.yaml into a contract. Validation starts once it succeeds.

docs.title: Layer 2: Cross-field
docs.text:
Validates semantic references and consistency:

Rule Code service.version parses as semver, leniently: 1, 0.1 and v0.1 all pass INVALID_SEMVER Interface names are unique DUPLICATE_INTERFACE_NAME interfaces[].lifecycle dates are strict YYYY-MM-DD and sunset is not before deprecated INVALID_INTERFACE_LIFECYCLE interfaces[].lifecycle.successor names another interface or is an absolute URL INTERFACE_SUCCESSOR_UNKNOWN Configuration names are unique DUPLICATE_CONFIGURATION_NAME Policy names are unique DUPLICATE_POLICY_NAME Dependency names are unique DUPLICATE_DEPENDENCY_NAME Interface spec file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND Interface spec file parses, if the ref ends .json, .yaml or .yml (for any other extension, only existence is checked) INVALID_INTERFACE_SPEC An mcp interface file lists tools, each with a name used once INVALID_MCP_TOOLS Check names are unique DUPLICATE_CHECK_NAME checks[].file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND extension capability ref is well-formed CAPABILITY_REF_INVALID Each standard capability type is declared once DUPLICATE_CAPABILITY capabilities[].binding.interface matches a declared interface CAPABILITY_INTERFACE_UNKNOWN capabilities[].binding.path is a safe application path CAPABILITY_PATH_INVALID OCI dependency refs (oci://) are valid OCI references INVALID_OCI_REF A dependency without ref is external DEPENDENCY_REF_REQUIRED An external dependency without ref has a version EXTERNAL_VERSION_REQUIRED compatibility appears only with ref, and version only without it COMPATIBILITY_WITHOUT_REF, VERSION_WITH_REF A dependency with ref has a compatibility range EMPTY_COMPATIBILITY Compatibility ranges are valid semver constraints INVALID_COMPATIBILITY OCI dependency pins a digest TAG_NOT_DIGEST (warning) configurations[].ref is a valid OCI reference INVALID_CONFIG_REF configurations[].schema file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND configurations[].schema file is valid JSON INVALID_CONFIG_JSON configurations[].schema file is valid JSON Schema INVALID_CONFIG_SCHEMA configurations[].values match the schema CONFIG_VALUES_VALIDATION_FAILED policies[].schema file exists in the bundle FILE_NOT_FOUND policies[].schema file is valid JSON INVALID_POLICY_JSON policies[].schema file is valid JSON Schema INVALID_POLICY_SCHEMA policies[].ref is a valid OCI reference INVALID_POLICY_REF Environment names are unique DUPLICATE_ENVIRONMENT_NAME environments[].file is a path in the bundle and the file exists FILE_NOT_FOUND readiness.claims[].id are unique within the contract DUPLICATE_READINESS_ID readiness.claims[].evidence has non-whitespace content EMPTY_READINESS_EVIDENCE readiness.claims[].description (when present) has non-whitespace content EMPTY_READINESS_DESCRIPTION readiness.expires is a strict YYYY-MM-DD date INVALID_READINESS_EXPIRES readiness.history[].{date,version,author,description} are valid/non-blank INVALID_READINESS_REVISION

This table lists the codes you can see. Layer 1 rejects the contract first and reports SCHEMA_VIOLATION wherever the JSON Schema already constrains a field. That covers the interface and capability type enums, a non-empty interfaces[].ref or dependencies[].compatibility, the configurations[] schema/ref choice, policies[].target and the stateless/ephemeral invariant. Layer 2 has its own check for each of those, but a contract that breaks them never gets past Layer 1. Build CI rules only on codes in this table.

docs.title: Layer 3: Policy checks
docs.text:
Resolves every declared policy and checks the contract against it. Policies apply with strict AND semantics: the contract must satisfy all of them. Policies have no precedence or override logic, so contradictory policies fail.

Condition Code policies[].ref cannot be resolved (resolver unavailable, network error, bundle not found) POLICY_REF_UNRESOLVED Cycle detected in recursive policy resolution chain POLICY_REF_CYCLE Contract violates a policy constraint POLICY_VIOLATION policies[].ref was skipped because no resolver was configured POLICY_REF_NOT_ENFORCED (warning)

POLICY_REF_UNRESOLVED is a hard error. Validation fails closed when a referenced policy cannot be resolved.

When ref-based policies are resolved. Recursive resolution of policies[].ref happens only when a resolver is configured. pacto validate and pacto push both supply one, since they can reach OCI/file refs. A ref policy that cannot be fetched then fails closed with POLICY_REF_UNRESOLVED, which is how pacto push checks remote policies before publishing. pacto pack and the operator pass no resolver. They check only the locally compiled schema-based policies and skip ref policies, so they never report the unresolved error. Cycle detection is per chain: a ref is a cycle only when it reappears in its own resolution chain (A → B → A); two sibling policies pointing at the same ref resolve independently.

docs.title: Dependency closure
docs.text:
By default Layer 3 checks the root contract only. pacto validate --closure also checks every contract in the dependency closure against the policies the root resolves. Each dependency's own policies[] is left to its owner's validation. The closure resolves the same way pacto graph does, with one fetch per dependency. External dependencies carry no contract and are skipped.

Condition Code A dependency violates a policy the root resolves CLOSURE_POLICY_VIOLATION A dependency cannot be resolved, sits in a dependency cycle or has an unreadable contract CLOSURE_DEPENDENCY_UNRESOLVED A direct dependency declares a deprecated interface DEPENDENCY_INTERFACE_DEPRECATED (warning) That interface has reached its sunset DEPENDENCY_INTERFACE_SUNSET (warning)

A policy finding names the dependency in its path, for example dependencies[ledger@1.0.0]. A dependency that cannot be resolved is named in the message. When a dependency declared it, the path names that dependency. An unresolvable dependency fails the run, so the check fails closed.

A deprecated interface is a warning that names the interface, its sunset and its successor, with the path of the dependency that resolved to it, for example dependencies[1]. Both codes stay warnings so the verdict does not change with the date the check runs. To fail a pipeline after the sunset, gate on DEPENDENCY_INTERFACE_SUNSET in --output-format json. When pacto.lock is present, the lock is verified first and a drifted closure fails with the lock error before the closure is checked.

docs.title: Environments stage
docs.text:
After the policy layer, the environments stage checks each environment's file against the schema of every configuration it names. It runs only when every stage before it passed, and reports SKIP no environments declared for a contract without environments. Environments lists the rules and the codes it reports: ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION, ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_INVALID, ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_MISSING and the ENVIRONMENT_VALUES_UNVERIFIED warning.

An error in an environment's file carries that file in file, with line and column pointing into it, also when --set or -f is given. The stage passes only when Pacto checked every value set and found no error. A configuration whose schema is behind a ref leaves its values unchecked, and so does a run with no bundle files to read, such as the operator loading an inline contract. A stage with no error and an unchecked value set reports SKIP could not verify: and names each environment and configuration.
