Conditions say what the state is; the Events: block that closes kubectl describe pacto <name> says what changed, including things no field records, such as a tag force-pushed underneath you or a readiness gate flipping.

kubectl describe pacto <name>                       # events are the last block
kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=<name> \
  --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

The operator emits exactly eight, and no others:

Reason Type Emitted when What it tells you ContractInvalid Warning The contract was obtained and judged invalid Carries the same message as the ContractValid / Invalid condition. Fix the contract. ContractUnavailable Warning The contract could not be obtained at all Registry unreachable, auth rejected, tag missing. See Contract not resolving. ValidationFailed Warning A contract that did load ends the reconcile as anything but Compliant or Reference, and the status differs from the one the previous reconcile persisted Carries the counts -- ContractStatus: NonCompliant, 2 errors, 1 warnings. status.findings names each one. ContractRecovered Normal The contract status returned to Compliant or Reference from any other value The other half of the three warnings above. RevisionCreated Normal A PactoRevision was created for a newly resolved contract Created revision <name> for contract v<version>. Expected on the first resolve and on every version change; not a problem. TagOverwritten Warning A tag that already resolved now points at a different digest Someone force-pushed the tag. See Choosing a reference form. ReadinessGateUnmet Warning The readiness gate went from met to unmet The message breaks the score down by claim status. ReadinessRecovered Normal The readiness gate went from unmet to met The other half of the pair above.

Three things about them are easy to misread:

  • ValidationFailed overstates the Unknown case. In that case an assertion could not be evaluated, and the event's own counts say so: ContractStatus: Unknown, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Trust the counts over the reason.
  • Every event except RevisionCreated and TagOverwritten is transition-gated. A contract that stays broken emits one event for the whole streak, so a Count above 1 means the status flapped, or the same reason recurred after a recovery. Two exceptions still repeat without either: TagOverwritten (see Choosing a reference form) and a revision-mirror failure, which is recorded once per reconcile pass.
  • Events expire, after the API server's --event-ttl of one hour by default. A missing event may have expired, so rely on conditions and status as the durable record.

docs.title: Chasing the evidence behind a finding
docs.text:
Every finding carries evidenceRefs, and this is what they contain:

evidenceRefs:
  - source: k8s
    observedAt: "2026-08-22T21:31:04Z"
    collector: k8s-observer
    detectedAt: "2026-08-22T21:31:04Z"

That is the whole record: which collector saw it and when. collector is k8s-observer for the Kubernetes API alone, k8s-observer+ebpf when node agent evidence decided or qualified the result and ebpf when only the kernel saw it. A finding with no matched observation, such as EVIDENCE_MISSING, carries source and observedAt only. The operator's observations are recomputed every reconcile and never stored, so the reference dates the reading and has no body to fetch. The node agent's raw socket view is the one exception you can read back, in the NodeRuntimeObservation object named after the pod's node. What it is good for is age: an observedAt that stopped advancing while metadata.generation moved on is a leftover from a reconcile that no longer runs.

To re-observe, nudge the resource. Any update enqueues a reconcile, and the annotation key is arbitrary:

kubectl annotate pacto <name> reconcile-requested-at="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" --overwrite

For observations that must outlive the reconcile that made them, such as an audit trail or a signed record, use the Evidence Server, which writes to your registry. Cluster status is a live reading.

docs.title: Status is Unknown
docs.text:
A required assertion could not be evaluated. This is uncertainty, and the finding code says why:

  • EVIDENCE_MISSING: nothing was collected. The target may not exist yet, or spec.target.serviceName does not match a real Service.
  • OBSERVATION_UNSUPPORTED: the dimension cannot be observed here: an ExternalName dependency, or a metrics capability while --enable-metrics-observation is off.
  • COLLECTION_FAILED: the cluster query errored, or the node agent could not load its kernel program. Check the RuntimeObserved condition and the operator logs.
  • EVIDENCE_STALE: the node agent on the pod's node stopped reporting. See Node agent evidence is missing.
  • EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT: some evidence arrived but not enough to decide, for example the node agent saw only part of a pod.

A contract that could not be obtained transiently also reads Unknown rather than Invalid.

docs.title: Status is Invalid
docs.text:
Structural validation failed or the artifact could not be parsed (fail-closed). status.validation carries the SCHEMA_VIOLATION or parse error; reproduce it locally:

pacto validate oci://ghcr.io/your-org/my-service-pacto:1.2.0

docs.title: Status is NonCompliant
docs.text: At least one confirmed violation. The two configuration codes do not arrive at the same speed. A mismatch (CONFIGURATION_MISMATCH) is NonCompliant on the first reconcile that observes it. An absence (CONFIGURATION_ABSENT) reads Unknown until the negative streak spans the stabilization window.

docs.title: Status is Reference
docs.text: The contract declares no spec.target: Pacto parses and validates it and observes nothing. Add a spec.target to enable runtime observation.

docs.title: Contract not resolving
docs.text:
• Confirm the OCI reference is reachable and, for private registries, that a pull secret is set via spec.contractRef.pullSecretRef.
  • For an unversioned reference the operator tracks the highest semver tag; a registry with no valid semver tags resolves nothing.
  • Inspect the created PactoRevision resources: kubectl get pactorevisions.

docs.title: Metrics or health always Unknown
docs.text:
The metrics dimension returns Unsupported unless --enable-metrics-observation is set, and active health probing requires --enable-probing. The chart sets them through controller.enableMetricsObservation and controller.enableProbing; see Opt-in features.

With probing off, health falls back to the workload, which needs an httpGet readiness probe on the container behind the health capability's port plus a Ready endpoint for it. When the capability declares a path, the probe's path must equal it. A liveness-only pod, an exec or tcpSocket probe or no probe leaves nothing to read. Passive observation can confirm health but never contradict it, so the answer here is Unknown.

docs.title: Operator RBAC errors
docs.text: If the logs show forbidden errors reading Services, workloads or EndpointSlices, confirm the operator's ClusterRole is installed. See RBAC. The chart adds read access to ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor only when controller.enableMetricsObservation is on. If you set the controller flag by hand instead, grant that access yourself, as Opt-in features shows.

docs.title: Node agent evidence is missing
docs.text:
The node agent is the optional DaemonSet (one pod per node) behind runtime conformance. If findings never carry collector: k8s-observer+ebpf, check these in order:

kubectl -n pacto-node-agent get daemonset pacto-node-agent
kubectl -n pacto-node-agent get noderuntimeobservations,leases
kubectl -n pacto-operator-system logs deploy/pacto-operator | grep node-agent
  • No DaemonSet. nodeAgent.enabled is off, or the agent runs in another nodeAgent.namespace.
  • DaemonSet with no pods. Something rejects them in the agent namespace. The operator sets its Pod Security labels to privileged at every sync; read kubectl -n pacto-node-agent describe daemonset pacto-node-agent for the admission message, for example from a policy engine of your own.
  • Pods running, no NodeRuntimeObservation or Lease for a node. That node's findings read EVIDENCE_STALE. Read the agent pod's log on that node. A write refused with may only write the objects named after its node or carries no node name comes from the chart's admission policy: the agent's token does not name its node, which needs Kubernetes 1.30 or later.
  • A Lease older than its node's observation. The Lease is the heartbeat; the operator reads whichever of its renewTime and the observation's lastPublished is newer.
  • Collection Failed. The kernel could not load the program, often because it lacks BTF (the kernel type information at /sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux). A kernel older than 5.11 can also fail to load it when the container runtime's RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is too low for its maps. Turn it on lists what each node needs.

docs.title: Delivery records are not written
docs.text:
With the recorder on, every Stage carries a RecordStoreReady condition. Read its reason:

kubectl get stages.delivery.pacto.trianalab.io -A \
  -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RECORDS:.status.conditions[?(@.type=="RecordStoreReady")].reason

ReferrersUnsupported means the streams repository's registry does not serve the OCI Referrers API, and the message starts with the registry has no Referrers API. The recorder has no tag fallback, so the Stage stays below the automatic levels. GHCR and released distribution behave this way. Move delivery.recorder.streamsRepository, and the versions and contracts your Stages apply, to a registry that serves the API natively, such as zot. Check it works lists the other reasons.

docs.title: Upgrade the Kubernetes operator
docs.text:
An upgrade is one helm upgrade, which updates the CRDs along with the operator. A cluster whose CRDs came from an older chart's crds/ directory needs one extra step the first time, and this page shows it.

The Kubernetes integration has its own version, separate from Pacto core: the operator image, Helm chart, Go module and these docs move together.

docs.title: Upgrade with Helm
docs.text:
The currently published chart:

helm upgrade pacto-operator \
  oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator \
  --version 6.4.0 \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system

An upgrade reverts hand-patched controller flags

helm upgrade rebuilds the Deployment's args from the chart, so a flag you patched in by hand disappears without an error. Set opt-in features through chart values such as controller.enableProbing, controller.enableMetricsObservation and nodeAgent.enabled, which survive an upgrade. A flag with no chart value, such as name-match discovery, has to be patched again after every upgrade; see Limitations: opt-in features.

docs.title: Hand older CRDs to Helm
docs.text:
A CRD (CustomResourceDefinition) tells Kubernetes what a Pacto object looks like. The chart renders its CRDs as part of the release, so helm upgrade updates a changed CRD and adds a new one, and helm uninstall keeps them (helm.sh/resource-policy: keep). Older charts installed the operator CRDs from a crds/ directory that Helm never upgrades and never records as part of the release.

If your CRDs came from such a chart, helm upgrade stops with invalid ownership metadata. Label and annotate them for your release once, then run the upgrade. Change the release name and namespace if yours differ:

for crd in $(kubectl get crd -o name | grep -E '/[a-z]+\.pacto\.trianalab\.io$'); do
  kubectl label "$crd" app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm --overwrite
  kubectl annotate "$crd" --overwrite \
    meta.helm.sh/release-name=pacto-operator \
    meta.helm.sh/release-namespace=pacto-operator-system
done

The loop runs the same in bash and zsh. The grep matches only the operator CRDs. The delivery CRDs, group delivery.pacto.trianalab.io, were already part of the release.

docs.title: Image values
docs.text:
The chart builds each image from global.imageRegistry (default ghcr.io) and a repository without a registry, such as trianalab/pacto/operator. An image's own registry value replaces the global one for that image.

Values from older charts set the whole reference in image.repository or delivery.image.repository, such as ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto-operator/pacto-controller. The chart keeps such a repository as the whole reference and adds no registry, so these values upgrade unchanged. The chart treats a repository as already carrying a registry host when its first path segment holds a . or : or is localhost. The Helm reference lists every image value.

docs.title: Upgrading across a major version (CRD migration)
docs.text:
Helm applies the new CRDs ahead of the new operator, so a major upgrade is the same command as any other:

helm upgrade pacto-operator \
  oci://ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/charts/pacto-operator \
  --version 6.4.0 \
  --namespace pacto-operator-system

The API version stays v1alpha1 across the major bump and the stored version is unchanged. Every existing Pacto resource therefore remains stored and readable under the new CRD, with no conversion webhook and no decode error, and the upgraded operator reconciles it in place. That holds because spec is additive: v5 adds spec.target.configBindings and spec.target.interfaceBindings and removes nothing, so a contract resource written for v4 still validates unchanged.

docs.title: Status is redesigned
docs.text:
The upgrade drops v4 status observations on sight

v5 redesigns status: it removes 51 status paths and adds 35. status.runtime, status.endpoints, status.ports, status.scaling, status.readiness.checks, status.contract.imageRef and status.summary.{passed,failed,total} are gone, replaced by status.findings, status.evaluationCoverage and status.summary.{errorCount,warningCount,infoCount,unknownCount}. That is why the printer columns change from PASSED/FAILED to ERRORS/WARNINGS.

The apiserver stops serving the removed fields the moment the new CRD lands. A kubectl get pacto -o yaml taken before the new operator writes status therefore shows a resource whose spec is intact and whose status looks half-empty. The CRD causes this. The old values are still in etcd and are lost for good only once something writes status again, so that window is a normal part of the migration.

docs.title: Confirming the migration
docs.text:
Before and after the upgrade:

kubectl get crd pactos.pacto.trianalab.io \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[0].additionalPrinterColumns[*].name}'   # reflects the new schema
kubectl get pacto -A                                                    # existing resources still list + reconcile

If a future release ever ships an incompatible schema change, the upgrade or the resource read fails with an error, so no resource disappears silently. See the CRD reference for the current field set.

This exact flow is exercised against a real cluster by tests/acceptance/kind/upgrade-v4-v5.sh, the upgrade leg of CI's ci-e2e-kind job. It installs the real v4 chart with its v4 CRDs, hands them to Helm as above, then helm upgrades to the current chart and asserts the CRDs migrate and the pre-existing resource survives and reconciles.

docs.title: Upgrading to v6
docs.text:
v6 adds the NodeRuntimeObservation CRD, which helm upgrade creates. Hand the older CRDs to Helm first as above, then check these before helm upgrade:

  • Removed flags and values. --webhook-cert-path, --webhook-cert-name, --webhook-cert-key and --dashboard-oci-secret are gone; the operator refuses to start with an unknown flag. Replace dashboard.ociSecret: <name> with dashboard.ociSecrets: [<name>]: the chart schema rejects the old key.
  • The node agent has its own namespace. It runs in nodeAgent.namespace (pacto-node-agent by default), which the chart creates privileged for Pod Security. Drop the pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged label you may have put on the release namespace for it. At its first sync the operator deletes the agent it ran in the release namespace. A private pull secret for the agent image must exist in the agent namespace too.
  • RBAC is split by namespace. The managed components' lifecycle permissions moved from the ClusterRole to a Role in the release namespace and, with the node agent, a Role in the agent namespace. The chart renders both. An operator installed without the chart needs them added by hand (RBAC lists every rule).
  • Kernel evidence namespace. controller.kernelEvidence.namespace defaults to the agent namespace instead of the operator's.

docs.title: Delivery always installs its admission policies
docs.text:
Delivery no longer runs without its admission policies. The chart refuses delivery.admissionPolicies.enabled and delivery.admissionPolicies.allowUnguarded whatever their value, and names the replacement. Before helm upgrade:

  • Delete both keys from your values.
  • If you set allowUnguarded to skip the Kubernetes 1.30 and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API check for helm lint or helm template, set delivery.admissionPolicies.skipCapabilityCheck=true instead. The policies still render.
  • An upgrade that reuses the earlier release's values carries enabled: true over from the earlier chart's defaults, so it fails. Reuse them with --reset-then-reuse-values.

A promoter started without --admission-policies admits no operation and counts no approval.

docs.title: Rolling back
docs.text: Within a major, helm rollback pacto-operator reverts what the chart owns and leaves your Pacto resources untouched; re-apply any hand-patched controller flags afterwards. Across a major it takes more work. A chart from before the CRDs moved into the release does not carry them, so rolling back to it leaves the new CRDs in place. The old controller then writes status fields the new schema lacks, which the API server drops while still reporting success. A real return to that major means rolling the chart back and server-side applying the previous release's CRDs from its config/crd/bases.

docs.title: Turning on the Evidence Server during an upgrade
docs.text: The Evidence Server arrived in chart 5.2.0 and is off by default, so an upgrade changes nothing until you set evidence.enabled. Its requirements, a subject list and a registry serving the native Referrers API, are on The Evidence Server. Turning it back off later removes the whole footprint and loses nothing: every accepted record already lives in your contract registry.

docs.title: Version compatibility
docs.text:
The Kubernetes integration is versioned independently from Pacto core. The table below is generated from integration.yaml and release/release-manifest.json.

Integration artifact Version Supported Pacto core Operator image 6.4.0 >=4.0.0 Operator chart 6.4.0 >=4.0.0 Delivery image 6.4.0 >=4.0.0 Go module 6.4.0 >=4.0.0 Integration docs 6.4.0 >=4.0.0

Contracts with pactoVersion: "2.1" need Pacto core 4.1.0 or later and operator 6.1.0 or later. Contracts with pactoVersion: "2.2" need Pacto core 4.3.0 or later and operator 6.3.0 or later. Contracts with pactoVersion: "2.3" need Pacto core 4.4.0 or later and operator 6.4.0 or later.

This documentation set corresponds to Pacto core 4.4.0. The integration's own version (currently operator/chart 6.4.0, docs 6.4.0) advances on its own release cadence.

docs.title: Version selector
docs.text: The site version selector (top of the page) tracks Pacto core releases. Because the Kubernetes integration ships on its own cadence, a Kubernetes-only release does NOT add a new core version entry to the selector: it republishes the current core version in place with regenerated integration docs, and this compatibility table shows the integration version those docs describe. Pick a core version from the selector to read the integration docs that shipped with it.

docs.title: Published artifacts

docs.title: Verify a published artifact
docs.text:
The controller image, the opt-in delivery image and the Helm chart are signed keylessly by the release workflow through GitHub's OIDC issuer. Verify each one before installing it:

cosign verify \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/TrianaLab/pacto/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  ghcr.io/trianalab/pacto/operator:6.4.0

Anything other than a successful verification -- including no signatures found -- means do not deploy it. Not every Pacto artifact is signed; see what is signed and what is not.

docs.title: Contract bindings
docs.text: A Pacto resource points at a platform-agnostic contract (inline or in OCI) and binds it to concrete Kubernetes resources to observe. The binding fields below are generated from the Pacto CRD schema.

docs.title: Contract source (spec.contractRef)
docs.text: Field Type Required Enum Description spec.contractRef object yes ContractRef specifies where to find the Pacto contract. spec.contractRef.inline string no Inline allows specifying the contract YAML directly (for testing/dev). spec.contractRef.oci string no OCI is the OCI registry reference for the contract bundle. Three forms are supported: - Unversioned (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto): tracks the latest semver tag. - Tagged (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto:1.2.3): pinned to that exact tag. - Digest (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto@sha256:...): immutable, exact reference. spec.contractRef.pullSecretRef string no PullSecretRef is the name of a Secret in the same namespace containing OCI registry credentials. Supported secret types: - Opaque with "token" key (bearer token) - Opaque with "username"+"password" keys (basic auth) - kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson (standard Docker registry auth) For Opaque secrets, add a "registry" key (e.g. "ghcr.io") to bind the credentials to that host; the operator then refuses to send them to any other registry. Recommended to prevent a contract from redirecting a referenced secret to an attacker-controlled registry.

docs.title: Runtime target (spec.target)
docs.text:
When spec.target is omitted the Pacto is reference-only: the operator parses and validates the contract but performs no runtime observation.

Field Type Required Enum Description spec.target object no Target specifies which Kubernetes resources to observe. When omitted, the Pacto acts as a reference-only contract (no runtime validation). spec.target.configBindings []object no ConfigBindings maps contract configurations to the concrete ConfigMap/Secret backing each (B7). spec.target.configBindings[].configuration string yes Configuration is the contract configurations[].name this binding backs. spec.target.configBindings[].format string no yaml, json Format of the value at Key. Required with Key for ConfigMap conformance. spec.target.configBindings[].key string no Key names the single ConfigMap/Secret key to decode and validate. Omit for existence-only. spec.target.configBindings[].kind string yes ConfigMap, Secret Kind of the backing object. spec.target.configBindings[].name string yes Name of the backing ConfigMap/Secret in the Pacto's namespace. spec.target.interfaceBindings []object no InterfaceBindings maps contract interfaces to the Service port that serves each (B4). Kubernetes deployment knowledge, so it lives on the CR and the contract stays platform-agnostic. spec.target.interfaceBindings[].interface string yes Interface is the contract interfaces[].name this binding resolves. spec.target.interfaceBindings[].servicePort object yes ServicePort is the Service port name or number that serves the interface. spec.target.serviceName string no ServiceName is the name of the Kubernetes Service to observe. spec.target.workloadRef object no WorkloadRef identifies the workload (Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, or CronJob). If omitted, defaults to name=serviceName, kind=Deployment. spec.target.workloadRef.kind string no Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, CronJob Kind of the workload resource. Left unspecified (empty) unless the author sets it explicitly; WORKLOAD_MISMATCH only fires when BOTH name AND kind were explicit (AR7). No default is applied here so the collector can distinguish "author asserted kind X" from "kind was defaulted for the GET". spec.target.workloadRef.name string yes Name of the workload resource.

docs.title: Overrides (spec.overrides)
docs.text: Field Type Required Enum Description spec.overrides object no Overrides specifies partial configuration overrides to apply on top of the resolved contract. This enables environment-specific tuning without duplicating the entire contract inline. Semantics mirror the Pacto CLI --set / -f override model. spec.overrides.configurations []object no Configurations lists per-scope configuration value overrides. Each entry is matched by name to a configurations[] entry in the resolved contract. spec.overrides.configurations[].name string yes Name identifies the configuration scope to override (must match a configurations[] entry in the contract). spec.overrides.configurations[].values object yes Values contains the configuration key-value pairs to merge into the resolved contract. These values take precedence over the values declared in the contract.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A Pacto binding an OCI contract to a Service, with an interface bound to a named Service port and a configuration bound to a ConfigMap:

apiVersion: pacto.trianalab.io/v1alpha1
kind: Pacto
metadata:
  name: orders-api
  namespace: shop
spec:
  contractRef:
    oci: ghcr.io/acme/orders-api-pacto:1.2.0
  target:
    serviceName: orders-api
    interfaceBindings:
      - interface: http
        servicePort: http
    configBindings:
      - configuration: default
        kind: ConfigMap
        name: orders-api-config
        key: app.yaml
        format: yaml

docs.title: Choosing a reference form
docs.text:
The three contractRef.oci forms are not three styles. They decide what the binding means over time, and the operator records which one it inferred in status.resolutionPolicy -- PinnedDigest, PinnedTag or Latest.

  • Digest (...@sha256:<digest>) is the only form whose meaning cannot change. Every reconcile re-reads the same bytes, so a compliance verdict is reproducible: what the operator asserted last Tuesday is what it asserts today. The cost is real -- publishing a contract revision becomes a change to the Pacto resource too.
  • Tag (...:1.2.3) is a mutable name you control. If someone force-pushes that tag, the operator records a new PactoRevision and emits a TagOverwritten Warning Event naming the old and new digests. It still accepts the new content. Choose a tag when you want a promotable pointer and will treat that Event as a signal.
  • Unversioned (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto) re-resolves the highest semver tag on every reconcile -- every spec.checkIntervalSeconds, 300 by default. It fits an environment whose job is to run whatever is newest, such as a staging namespace or a preview cluster. It fits production badly, because what is being asserted changes without anyone deciding to change it.

With no other constraint: digest in production, unversioned in staging. The middle form is for teams that already run a tag-promotion discipline.

This page covers the binding fields only. The rest of spec -- including checkIntervalSeconds, which sets how often the operator re-checks compliance (default 300) -- is in the CRD reference.

A model the runner names that no such version matches fails the check either way. spec.gates.verify.checks[].suite string no Suite names a check the version's contract ships (its checks[].name) for an eval provider to run; without it the provider runs the only check the version ships. A version whose contract ships no check of that name, or with no suite ships none or more than one, is held for a person before it ships. spec.gates.verify.checks[].suiteDigest string no SuiteDigest pins the suite's bytes ("sha256:" and 64 hex digits). A version whose suite has another digest changed its own exam: it is held for a person before it ships, and an eval check of it is Unknown. spec.gates.verify.recheck string no Recheck is how often the verify gates run again on the version the Stage runs once it shipped (a Go duration, default 1m). A confirmed Fail rolls it back; Unknown never does. spec.gates.verify.window string no Window is how long the verify gates may stay Unknown before the operation is held for a human (a Go duration, default 5m). Re-checks after release judge the same length of time. spec.records object no RecordsPolicy says whether automation may move the Stage while its records cannot be written. spec.records.required boolean no Required holds every promote or rollback an agent or the promoter raises for a person to approve while the recorder is not writing this Stage's records (RecordStoreReady is not True) or more than five of its operations wait for a record (MaxRecordsPending). spec.service object yes ServiceRef is the Pacto ServiceID a Stage delivers: the domain-qualified service name its contracts declare. spec.service.domain string no Domain is the registry and organisation scope (empty for the default). spec.service.name string yes Name is the contract's service.name. spec.startLevel string no "observe" observe, advise, auto-nonbreaking, autonomous StartLevel is where a new Stage begins. It is read once, when status.level is empty; after that only an autonomy operation moves the level. Creating a Stage is an admin action, so any level is accepted, and a Stage whose status is lost seeds back to this level. Only observe and advise keep Pacto from shipping without a person. spec.workload object no Workload is the workload the service runs as, in the Stage's namespace: the one object pacto.contract and pacto.runtime may judge. The Pacto resource ships inside every version and names its own target, so without this a version could point its own check at a decoy. Empty is the Deployment named spec.service.name. spec.workload.kind string yes Kind is the workload kind, such as Deployment or StatefulSet. spec.workload.name string yes status object no StageStatus is written by the promoter's operation and stage reconcilers and by the recorder (Stream.Head, Stream.Anchor and RecordStoreReady), each through a compare-and-swap on the Stage's resourceVersion. status.authFreshness string no AuthFreshness is how old a login the promoter accepts on an approval (a Go duration). Clients ask for a fresh login with a margin under it (DecisionFreshnessFor). Empty: no login is too old, and a person decides with the session they have. status.autoHold boolean no AutoHold stops auto-promotion after a person or agent rolled back or promoted back to a version the Stage already verified. status.candidate string no Candidate is the newest eligible candidate the stage reconciler saw. status.conditions []object no Conditions holds Ready. It is False, naming what is missing, when the Stage cannot promote: its applier cannot be read, lacks the apply-ref label or (on Argo CD) has no single OCI source or no automated sync; its candidate OCIRepository does not exist or sets no spec.verify naming the publisher; the records of its upstream in another cluster are not trusted or cannot be read; or it names no candidate source at all. The recorder adds RecordStoreReady: False when the registry has no Referrers API, cannot be reached or holds a stream it refuses to fork. status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime string no LastTransitionTime is when Status last changed (RFC 3339). status.conditions[].message string no status.conditions[].observedGeneration integer no ObservedGeneration is the Stage generation the condition was set from. status.conditions[].reason string no status.conditions[].status string yes True, False, Unknown status.conditions[].type string yes status.failedDigests []string no FailedDigests are the last 50 versions that failed here; none of them is promoted again. An older failure drops out. status.frozen boolean no status.frozenReason string no status.lastCheck object no LastCheck is the newest re-check of the running version after it shipped. status.lastCheck.at string yes At is when the gates ran (RFC 3339). status.lastCheck.digest string yes status.lastCheck.operation string yes Operation is the uid of the operation that shipped the version. status.lastCheck.verdicts []object no status.lastCheck.verdicts[].citation object no status.lastCheck.verdicts[].gate string yes status.lastCheck.verdicts[].message string no status.lastCheck.verdicts[].phase string yes pre, verify status.lastCheck.verdicts[].result string yes Pass, Fail, Unknown Result is a gate verdict. status.lastOp string no LastOp is the uid of the operation that last moved the pointer. status.level string no Level is the Stage's autonomy level. The stage reconciler seeds it from spec.startLevel; after that only an autonomy operation writes it. status.locks object no Locks maps a facet to the uid of the operation holding it. status.observedGeneration integer no ObservedGeneration is the Stage generation the stage reconciler last judged Ready from. status.observedRevision object no ObservedRevision is what GitOps' source reports while the Stage observes. status.observedRevision.digest string yes status.observedRevision.since string yes status.offered []string no Offered holds the digests a promote carried through pacto.published with a pass (not an accepted unknown) and that then verified here, oldest first (cap 50). Only these are offered to a downstream Stage. status.pointer string no Pointer is the digest the Stage moved the environment to. It is set when an operation holding the pointer lock starts to apply, before Flux or Argo CD runs it: Applied on that operation says when they did. status.proposal object no Proposal is the next level Pacto proposes, or why not yet. status.proposal.blockers []object no status.proposal.blockers[].kind string yes Kind is missing-contract, undeclared-range, unlabelled-apply-ref, no-observed-digest, no-record-store, needs-verified, needs-cleared-breaking, incident or partial-graph. status.proposal.blockers[].message string yes status.proposal.blockers[].subject string no Subject is the service, consumer or caller identity. status.proposal.evidence []string no Evidence names the digests or operation uids that earned it. status.proposal.level string no Level is empty while nothing is proposed. status.published []string no Published holds the candidate digests Flux verified the signature of on the candidate OCIRepository (spec.verify naming the publisher's identity), oldest first (cap 50). Only these are promoted from the OCIRepository. status.rolledBack []string no RolledBack holds the uids of the failed operations the promoter raised its one automatic rollback for, oldest first (cap 50). A failure listed here never gets a second one. status.shadow []object no Shadow holds the newest would-have decisions while the Stage observes, newest first. status.shadow[].candidate string yes status.shadow[].decision string no Decision is the floor's decision: approve or accept-unknown. status.shadow[].from string no status.shadow[].impactDigest string no status.shadow[].intentDigest string yes status.shadow[].observedAt string no ObservedAt is when GitOps' source reported this candidate (RFC 3339): not proof of rollout. status.shadow[].owners []string no status.shadow[].plannedAt string yes PlannedAt is when Pacto planned it (RFC 3339). status.shadow[].predicted string yes Prediction is what plan() expects the promoter to do. status.shadow[].question string no status.shadow[].verification string no Verification is the shadow verify on the observed digest. status.stream object no Stream numbers a Stage's concluded operations. status.stream.anchor string no Anchor is where the stream's records are listed: <repository>@. Only the recorder writes it. status.stream.concluded []object no Concluded are the newest operations given a seq, each with how it concluded, written in the compare-and-swap that took the seq. An operation whose own status write then failed concludes again from here: the same seq and outcome, never a second seq. status.stream.concluded[].cause string no Cause is the uid of the operation whose failure made the promoter raise this one: an automatic rollback, freeze or step-down. status.stream.concluded[].clearedBreaking boolean no ClearedBreaking is a promote of a change that is not NON_BREAKING whose impact verdict passed: every consumer accepts it. status.stream.concluded[].outcome string no Outcome is how a concluded operation ended. status.stream.concluded[].person boolean no Person is true when the operation carried an approval or a person raised it. status.stream.concluded[].reason string no Reason is "Code: message". status.stream.concluded[].seq integer yes status.stream.concluded[].type string no Type is the operation type. status.stream.concluded[].uid string yes status.stream.concluded[].verification string no Verification qualifies a Succeeded outcome. status.stream.head string no Head is the digest of the newest record in the stream. Only the recorder writes it. status.stream.id string no ID is <clusterID>/<namespace>/<name>; the cluster id is the kube-system namespace uid. status.stream.recordedSeq integer no RecordedSeq is the newest local seq the recorder wrote or adopted a record for. Only the recorder writes it. status.stream.seq integer no status.upstreamAcknowledged []string no UpstreamAcknowledged holds the ids of the unrecordable stand-ins in the upstream stream that a person on this Stage checked and acknowledged, oldest first (cap 50). They no longer stop the Stage offering. status.upstreamSeen object no UpstreamSeen is the newest record this Stage read from the upstream stream it follows (candidates.upstreamRecords). A later read that ends before it, or holds another record at its seq, offers nothing, so records removed from the upstream's tail never go unseen. status.upstreamSeen.record string yes Record is the record's id, the digest of its signed payload. status.upstreamSeen.seq integer yes status.upstreamSeen.stream string yes Stream is the stream id. status.verified []string no Verified holds the newest verified digests, oldest first (cap 10).

docs.text: Field Type Required Default Enum Description status object no status is the agent's published observation. status.agentVersion string no AgentVersion is the node agent build version. status.collection object no Collection is the health of the kernel collection. status.collection.droppedEvents integer no DroppedEvents is the cumulative number of kernel events lost because the ring buffer was full, since the agent started. status.collection.lastDropAt string no LastDropAt is when the agent last saw DroppedEvents increase. status.collection.lastResyncAt string no LastResyncAt is when the agent last completed a /proc baseline scan. status.collection.message string no Message is a human-readable explanation of a non-Running state. status.collection.reason string no Reason is a CamelCase machine-readable cause for a non-Running state. status.collection.state string yes Running, Degraded, Failed State is Running, Degraded or Failed. status.kernelRelease string no KernelRelease is the node's kernel release (uname -r). status.lastPublished string no LastPublished is the heartbeat: the time of the most recent publish. status.nodeName string no NodeName is the Kubernetes node this object describes. status.observingSince string no ObservingSince is when this agent process started. status.pods []object no Pods are the pods running on the node, sorted by UID. status.pods[].baselineAt string no BaselineAt is the last /proc scan that saw the pod. status.pods[].connections []object no Connections are the pod's outbound TCP peers within the retention window. status.pods[].connections[].address string yes Address is the peer IP address. status.pods[].connections[].failures integer no Failures counts handshakes that went from SYN_SENT straight to CLOSE (refused, reset or timed out). status.pods[].connections[].lastFailureAt string no LastFailureAt is the time of the most recent failure. status.pods[].connections[].lastSuccessAt string no LastSuccessAt is the time of the most recent success. status.pods[].connections[].port integer yes Port is the peer port. status.pods[].connections[].successes integer no Successes counts handshakes that reached ESTABLISHED. status.pods[].listeners []object no Listeners are the pod's TCP listening sockets. status.pods[].listeners[].address string no Address is the bound local address (0.0.0.0 or :: for all addresses). A loopback-only listener does not serve traffic sent to the pod IP. status.pods[].listeners[].family string yes IPv4, IPv6 Family is the socket address family. status.pods[].listeners[].port integer yes Port is the local (container) port. status.pods[].listeners[].process string no Process is the command name of the process that opened the listener, when the agent saw it happen (empty when only the /proc baseline knows it). status.pods[].netnsShared boolean no NetnsShared is true when the pod's network namespace is not its own (the host namespace for hostNetwork pods). Socket events in it cannot be attributed to the pod, so listeners and connections stay empty. status.pods[].observedSince string no ObservedSince is when the agent first mapped the pod's network namespace. status.pods[].truncated boolean no Truncated is true when a per-pod or per-node bound was hit, so listeners or connections may be missing entries. status.pods[].uid string yes UID is the pod UID, read from the pod's cgroup path. status.publishIntervalSeconds integer no PublishIntervalSeconds is how often the agent publishes; readers derive staleness from it.

docs.text: Field Type Required Default Enum Description spec object yes spec defines the desired state of PactoRevision. spec.pactoRef string yes PactoRef is the name of the parent Pacto resource that owns this revision. spec.serviceName string no ServiceName is the service name from the contract. spec.source object yes Source specifies where this revision's contract was loaded from. spec.source.digest string no Digest is the OCI manifest digest (sha256:...) at the time of resolution. Used to detect force-pushes (tag overwrites) on the registry. spec.source.inline boolean no Inline indicates the contract was provided inline (no external source). spec.source.oci string no OCI is the fully resolved OCI reference (including tag/digest). Example: ghcr.io/org/service-pacto:1.2.0 spec.version string yes Version is the contract version (from contract.service.version). status object no status defines the observed state of PactoRevision. status.conditions []object no conditions represent the current state of the PactoRevision resource. status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime string yes lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. status.conditions[].message string yes message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. status.conditions[].observedGeneration integer no observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. status.conditions[].reason string yes reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. status.conditions[].status string yes True, False, Unknown status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. status.conditions[].type string yes type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. status.contractHash string no ContractHash is the SHA-256 hash of the raw contract YAML. Used to detect content changes across versions. status.createdAt string no CreatedAt is the timestamp when this revision was first resolved. status.resolved boolean yes Resolved indicates whether this revision has been successfully resolved and parsed.

docs.title: Pacto
docs.text:
• API group: pacto.trianalab.io
  • Version: v1alpha1
  • Kind: Pacto
  • Plural: pactos
  • Scope: Namespaced

docs.title: Additional printer columns
docs.text: Name Type JSONPath Status string .status.contractStatus Service string .spec.target.serviceName Version string .status.contractVersion Errors integer .status.summary.errorCount Warnings integer .status.summary.warningCount Last Reconciled date .status.lastReconciledAt Age date .metadata.creationTimestamp

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Enum Description spec object yes spec defines the desired state of Pacto. spec.checkIntervalSeconds integer no 300 CheckIntervalSeconds controls how often the reconciler re-checks compliance. Defaults to 300 (5 minutes). spec.contractRef object yes ContractRef specifies where to find the Pacto contract. spec.contractRef.inline string no Inline allows specifying the contract YAML directly (for testing/dev). spec.contractRef.oci string no OCI is the OCI registry reference for the contract bundle. Three forms are supported: - Unversioned (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto): tracks the latest semver tag. - Tagged (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto:1.2.3): pinned to that exact tag. - Digest (ghcr.io/org/service-pacto@sha256:...): immutable, exact reference. spec.contractRef.pullSecretRef string no PullSecretRef is the name of a Secret in the same namespace containing OCI registry credentials. Supported secret types: - Opaque with "token" key (bearer token) - Opaque with "username"+"password" keys (basic auth) - kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson (standard Docker registry auth) For Opaque secrets, add a "registry" key (e.g. "ghcr.io") to bind the credentials to that host; the operator then refuses to send them to any other registry. Recommended to prevent a contract from redirecting a referenced secret to an attacker-controlled registry. spec.overrides object no Overrides specifies partial configuration overrides to apply on top of the resolved contract. This enables environment-specific tuning without duplicating the entire contract inline. Semantics mirror the Pacto CLI --set / -f override model. spec.overrides.configurations []object no Configurations lists per-scope configuration value overrides. Each entry is matched by name to a configurations[] entry in the resolved contract. spec.overrides.configurations[].name string yes Name identifies the configuration scope to override (must match a configurations[] entry in the contract). spec.overrides.configurations[].values object yes Values contains the configuration key-value pairs to merge into the resolved contract. These values take precedence over the values declared in the contract. spec.target object no Target specifies which Kubernetes resources to observe. When omitted, the Pacto acts as a reference-only contract (no runtime validation). spec.target.configBindings []object no ConfigBindings maps contract configurations to the concrete ConfigMap/Secret backing each (B7). spec.target.configBindings[].configuration string yes Configuration is the contract configurations[].name this binding backs. spec.target.configBindings[].format string no yaml, json Format of the value at Key. Required with Key for ConfigMap conformance. spec.target.configBindings[].key string no Key names the single ConfigMap/Secret key to decode and validate. Omit for existence-only. spec.target.configBindings[].kind string yes ConfigMap, Secret Kind of the backing object. spec.target.configBindings[].name string yes Name of the backing ConfigMap/Secret in the Pacto's namespace. spec.target.interfaceBindings []object no InterfaceBindings maps contract interfaces to the Service port that serves each (B4). Kubernetes deployment knowledge, so it lives on the CR and the contract stays platform-agnostic. spec.target.interfaceBindings[].interface string yes Interface is the contract interfaces[].name this binding resolves. spec.target.interfaceBindings[].servicePort object yes ServicePort is the Service port name or number that serves the interface. spec.target.serviceName string no ServiceName is the name of the Kubernetes Service to observe. spec.target.workloadRef object no WorkloadRef identifies the workload (Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, or CronJob). If omitted, defaults to name=serviceName, kind=Deployment. spec.target.workloadRef.kind string no Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, CronJob Kind of the workload resource. Left unspecified (empty) unless the author sets it explicitly; WORKLOAD_MISMATCH only fires when BOTH name AND kind were explicit (AR7). No default is applied here so the collector can distinguish "author asserted kind X" from "kind was defaulted for the GET". spec.target.workloadRef.name string yes Name of the workload resource. status object no status defines the observed state of Pacto. status.capabilities []object no Capabilities lists the declared capabilities from the contract. status.capabilities[].ref string no Ref is the capability reference (OCI URI or local path). status.capabilities[].type string yes Type is the capability type (e.g. "database", "cache"). status.conditions []object no Conditions represent aggregated state (ContractValid, RuntimeObserved, etc.). status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime string yes lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. status.conditions[].message string yes message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. status.conditions[].observedGeneration integer no observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. status.conditions[].reason string yes reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. status.conditions[].status string yes True, False, Unknown status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. status.conditions[].type string yes type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. status.configurations []object no Configurations lists the contract's named configuration scopes. Each entry corresponds to one configurations[] entry in the contract. status.configurations[].hasSchema boolean yes HasSchema indicates whether a JSON Schema file is bundled. status.configurations[].name string yes Name is the configuration scope name (required, unique within contract). status.configurations[].overriddenKeys []string no OverriddenKeys lists configuration keys whose values were overridden by spec.overrides.configurations. Empty when no overrides apply. status.configurations[].properties []object no Properties lists the configuration's declared keys with their type and default/value, extracted from the bundled schema (or literal values), so consumers can render configuration content without re-reading the bundle. status.configurations[].properties[].key string yes Key is the property name (dot-notation for nested objects). status.configurations[].properties[].type string no Type is the JSON Schema type of the property. status.configurations[].properties[].value string no Value is the default (for schema properties) or the literal value. status.configurations[].ref string no Ref is the external OCI reference for the configuration schema, if used. status.configurations[].secretKeys []string no SecretKeys lists configuration keys whose values reference secrets. status.configurations[].valueKeys []string no ValueKeys lists the declared configuration value keys. status.contract object no Contract exposes parsed contract metadata. status.contract.owner object no Owner contains the structured ownership metadata from the contract (team, DRI, and contacts). status.contract.owner.contacts []object no Contacts lists provider-neutral contact points. status.contract.owner.contacts[].purpose string no Purpose describes what this contact is used for (e.g. escalation, support, oncall). status.contract.owner.contacts[].type string yes Type is the contact channel type (e.g. email, chat, oncall). status.contract.owner.contacts[].value string yes Value is the contact address or identifier. status.contract.owner.dri string no DRI is the directly responsible individual. status.contract.owner.team string no Team is the owning team name. status.contract.ownerDisplay string no OwnerDisplay is the canonical display string derived from owner metadata. Precedence: team > DRI. Useful for printer columns, dashboards, and backward-compatible consumers. status.contract.resolvedRef string no ResolvedRef is the fully-resolved OCI reference (with tag/digest). Empty for inline contracts. status.contract.serviceName string yes ServiceName is the service name declared in the contract. status.contract.version string yes Version is the semver version from the contract. status.contractStatus string no Compliant, Warning, NonCompliant, Reference, Unknown, Invalid, NotEvaluated ContractStatus is the high-level contract compliance state. This reflects contract validation/compliance and is NOT runtime health. status.contractVersion string no ContractVersion is the version from the parsed contract. Kept for backward compatibility and simple access via JSONPath. status.currentRevision string no CurrentRevision is the name of the active PactoRevision. status.dependencies []object no Dependencies lists the declared dependencies from the contract. status.dependencies[].compatibility string no Compatibility is the semver constraint for the dependency. status.dependencies[].external boolean no External marks a dependency this Pacto system does not run, such as a managed database or a hosted model. status.dependencies[].name string yes Name is the dependency name (required, unique within contract). status.dependencies[].ref string no Ref is the dependency reference (OCI URI). Empty for an external dependency that has no contract. status.dependencies[].required boolean yes Required indicates whether this dependency is mandatory. status.dependencies[].requires []object no Requires lists the behavior this service relies on from the provider's interfaces. status.dependencies[].requires[].dedupeWindow string no DedupeWindow is how long a repeated message is recognised and dropped. status.dependencies[].requires[].delivery string no Delivery is what happens when a delivery fails partway. status.dependencies[].requires[].idempotent boolean no Idempotent means repeating a call has the effect of making it once. status.dependencies[].requires[].interface string yes Interface names the provider's interface. status.dependencies[].requires[].ordering string no Ordering is the scope in which messages arrive in the order sent. status.dependencies[].requires[].profile string no Profile is the version of the guarantee vocabulary. status.dependencies[].requires[].retention string no Retention is how long a message stays available for replay. status.dependencies[].requires[].timeout string no Timeout is the longest a call takes to answer. status.dependencies[].version string no Version is the free-text version an external dependency without a ref declares. status.evaluatedRevision object no EvaluatedRevision ties this status to the exact contract and workload generation it was computed from, so a result for an old version is never read as the answer for a new one. A consumer acting on contractStatus (the opt-in Pacto delivery promoter) must check it first. status.evaluatedRevision.contractDigest string no ContractDigest is the OCI manifest digest of the evaluated contract bundle. Empty for inline contracts. status.evaluatedRevision.kernelCoverage string no Complete, Partial, Failed, Stale KernelCoverage is how far the node agent's view of the workload's pods could be trusted in this evaluation, the worst pod first: Complete, Partial, Failed or Stale. Empty when kernel evidence is off. Complete is what lets a reader tell "observed and clean" from "not observed". status.evaluatedRevision.workload object no Workload is the workload object and generation the evaluation read. Absent for a reference-only contract or a workload that does not exist. status.evaluatedRevision.workload.generation integer yes status.evaluatedRevision.workload.kind string yes status.evaluatedRevision.workload.name string yes status.evaluatedRevision.workload.uid string yes status.evaluationCoverage object no EvaluationCoverage reports how many required assertions were evaluated (metadata; never affects ContractStatus). status.evaluationCoverage.evaluated integer yes Evaluated is the number of required assertions with a conclusive (Observed) observation. status.evaluationCoverage.required integer yes Required is the total number of required assertions the contract declares. status.evaluationCoverage.unverified []string no Unverified lists, sorted, the contract paths of declared facets that have a runtime check but no usable fact this time (for example interfaces[name=api].type with probing off). Metadata only: it never changes the contract status. status.findings []object no Findings is the list of typed conclusions from the Pacto engine. Includes both contract-only findings (structural/semantic) and evidence-based findings (runtime drift). status.findings[].category string yes Category groups related codes (e.g. RuntimeDrift, PolicyViolation). status.findings[].code string yes Code is the stable finding identifier (e.g. WORKLOAD_MISMATCH). status.findings[].contractPath string no ContractPath is the YAML path to the relevant contract field. status.findings[].evidenceRefs []object no EvidenceRefs links the finding to supporting evidence. status.findings[].evidenceRefs[].collector string no Collector names the producer of the matched observation: k8s-observer for the Kubernetes API alone, k8s-observer+ebpf when kernel evidence was merged in, ebpf when only the kernel saw it. status.findings[].evidenceRefs[].detectedAt string no DetectedAt is the RFC 3339 time the matched observation was made. status.findings[].evidenceRefs[].observedAt string yes ObservedAt is the ISO8601 timestamp when the evidence was collected. status.findings[].evidenceRefs[].source string yes Source is the evidence source (e.g. "k8s"). status.findings[].message string yes Message is a human-readable description. status.findings[].severity string yes error, warning, info, unknown Severity is error, warning, info, or unknown. status.findings[].subject string no Subject identifies what the finding is about. status.interfaces []object no Interfaces lists the parsed interfaces from the contract. status.interfaces[].compatibilityEpoch integer no CompatibilityEpoch is raised when the interface's behavior changes incompatibly while its specification stays the same. Absent is 0. status.interfaces[].guarantees object no Guarantees is the behavior the interface promises its consumers. status.interfaces[].guarantees.dedupeWindow string no DedupeWindow is how long a repeated message is recognised and dropped. status.interfaces[].guarantees.delivery string no Delivery is what happens when a delivery fails partway. status.interfaces[].guarantees.idempotent boolean no Idempotent means repeating a call has the effect of making it once. status.interfaces[].guarantees.ordering string no Ordering is the scope in which messages arrive in the order sent. status.interfaces[].guarantees.profile string no Profile is the version of the guarantee vocabulary. status.interfaces[].guarantees.retention string no Retention is how long a message stays available for replay. status.interfaces[].guarantees.timeout string no Timeout is the longest a call takes to answer. status.interfaces[].lifecycle object no Lifecycle is the retirement schedule of a deprecated interface. Absent for an interface that is not deprecated. status.interfaces[].lifecycle.deprecated string yes Deprecated is the date the interface was deprecated (YYYY-MM-DD). status.interfaces[].lifecycle.successor string no Successor names the interface that replaces this one, or holds an absolute URL when the replacement lives in another service. status.interfaces[].lifecycle.sunset string no Sunset is the date the interface is removed (YYYY-MM-DD). status.interfaces[].name string yes Name is the interface name. status.interfaces[].ref string no Ref is the bundle-relative path to the interface specification file. status.interfaces[].type string yes openapi, asyncapi, grpc, mcp Type is the interface type: openapi, asyncapi, grpc or mcp. status.interfaces[].visibility string no Visibility is the declared visibility: public or internal. status.lastReconciledAt string no LastReconciledAt is when the status was last written: on a change, and at least every half check interval while nothing changes. status.metadata object no Metadata contains arbitrary key-value pairs from the contract's metadata section. status.observationWindows []object no ObservationWindows tracks per-assertion negative-observation streaks for time-based stabilization (B5). Operator-owned temporal state; the pure engine never sees it. status.observationWindows[].firstObservedNegativeAt string yes FirstObservedNegativeAt is when the current negative streak began. status.observationWindows[].kind string yes Kind is the assertion dimension: interface | dependency | configuration | capability. status.observationWindows[].subject string yes Subject is the assertion identity (interface/dependency/configuration name, or capability key). status.observedCallers []object no ObservedCallers are workloads the node agent saw calling this target's Service, inside the dependency observation window, that no Pacto describes. Capped at 32, sorted by namespace, kind and name. status.observedCallers[].firstSeen string yes FirstSeen is set once, when the caller first appears, so the status does not change on every reconcile. status.observedCallers[].kind string yes Kind is the owning controller: Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob, another controller kind, or Pod for a pod no controller owns. status.observedCallers[].name string yes status.observedCallers[].namespace string yes status.observedCallers[].source string yes ebpf Source is the collector that saw the calls. status.observedCallersCoverage object no ObservedCallersCoverage says whether observedCallers can be trusted as complete. Absent when runtime observation is not configured for this Pacto. status.observedCallersCoverage.reason string no status.observedCallersCoverage.refreshSeconds integer no RefreshSeconds is how often the operator rewrites this status. A reader treats a status not reconciled within twice that as stale, so an operator that stopped never leaves a complete coverage in place. status.observedCallersCoverage.state string yes complete, partial, unavailable status.observedGeneration integer no ObservedGeneration is the most recent generation observed by the controller. status.observedRuntime object no ObservedRuntime describes the actual runtime state observed from the cluster. Only populated when a target workload exists. This is a lean evidence view. status.observedRuntime.containerImages []string no ContainerImages lists the container images from the pod spec. status.observedRuntime.deploymentStrategy string no DeploymentStrategy is the observed strategy (RollingUpdate, Recreate). Empty for non-Deployments. status.observedRuntime.hasEmptyDir boolean yes HasEmptyDir indicates whether the workload uses emptyDir volumes. status.observedRuntime.hasPVC boolean yes HasPVC indicates whether the workload uses PersistentVolumeClaims. status.observedRuntime.healthProbeInitialDelaySeconds integer no HealthProbeInitialDelaySeconds is the observed initialDelaySeconds from the first container's probe. status.observedRuntime.podManagementPolicy string no PodManagementPolicy is the observed pod management policy (OrderedReady, Parallel). Empty for non-StatefulSets. status.observedRuntime.terminationGracePeriodSeconds integer no TerminationGracePeriodSeconds is the observed terminationGracePeriodSeconds from the pod spec. status.observedRuntime.workloadKind string no WorkloadKind is the actual Kubernetes resource kind (Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, Job, CronJob). status.policies []object no Policies lists the contract's declared policy sources (metadata only). Each entry describes a local schema or external ref; the operator does not resolve or enforce ref-based policies at runtime. status.policies[].description string no Description is the policy schema's declared description, if any. status.policies[].hasSchema boolean yes HasSchema indicates whether a policy schema file is bundled. status.policies[].name string yes Name is the policy name (required, unique within contract). status.policies[].properties []object no Properties lists the policy schema's keys with their type and default, so consumers can render policy content without re-reading the bundle. status.policies[].properties[].key string yes Key is the property name (dot-notation for nested objects). status.policies[].properties[].type string no Type is the JSON Schema type of the property. status.policies[].properties[].value string no Value is the default (for schema properties) or the literal value. status.policies[].ref string no Ref is the external OCI reference for the policy schema, if used. status.policies[].schema string no Schema is the bundle-relative path to the policy schema file, if local. status.policies[].title string no Title is the policy schema's declared title, if any. status.readiness object no Readiness is the derived operational readiness assessment of the contract. It is computed from the contract's declared readiness claims and the current time. It is a separate dimension from contract compliance and does NOT affect ContractStatus. Absent when the contract declares no readiness. status.readiness.claims []object no Claims is the derived per-claim readiness status. status.readiness.claims[].category string no Category is the software-domain category (security, documentation, observability, etc.). status.readiness.claims[].description string no Description is the optional human-readable explanation. status.readiness.claims[].earnedWeight integer no EarnedWeight is the weight this check contributed toward the score. status.readiness.claims[].evidence string no Evidence is the declared pointer to the evidence. status.readiness.claims[].excluded boolean no Excluded reports whether the check is excluded from scoring (deferred). status.readiness.claims[].id string yes ID is the readiness requirement identifier (e.g. dashboard, runbook). status.readiness.claims[].status string yes done, partial, not-done, deferred Status is the declared completion status. status.readiness.claims[].type string yes Type classifies the evidence pointer (url, document, ticket, report, artifact, identifier, other). status.readiness.claims[].weight integer yes Weight is the declared contribution to the readiness score (0-100). status.readiness.daysRemaining integer no DaysRemaining is the number of whole days until expiry (nil when expired). status.readiness.deferredCount integer no DeferredCount is the number of checks declared deferred (excluded from scoring). status.readiness.doneCount integer no DoneCount is the number of checks declared done. status.readiness.earnedWeight integer no EarnedWeight is the weight earned toward the score. status.readiness.expired boolean no Expired reports whether the assessment has expired; when true every in-scope check earns 0. status.readiness.expires string no Expires is the assessment-level expiry boundary (YYYY-MM-DD). status.readiness.minScore integer no MinScore is the gate threshold (the declared readiness.minScore, or 100 when omitted). status.readiness.notDoneCount integer no NotDoneCount is the number of checks declared not-done. status.readiness.partialCount integer no PartialCount is the number of checks declared partial. status.readiness.passing boolean no Passing reports whether the gate is met (not expired and Score >= MinScore). status.readiness.revisions []object no Revisions is the declared readiness revision history. status.readiness.revisions[].author string yes Author is who performed the assessment. status.readiness.revisions[].date string yes Date is the date the revision was assessed (YYYY-MM-DD). status.readiness.revisions[].description string yes Description summarizes what changed or was observed. status.readiness.revisions[].version string yes Version is the service version assessed in this revision. status.readiness.score integer no Score is the percentage of in-scope weight earned (0-100). status.readiness.totalWeight integer no TotalWeight is the sum of in-scope (non-deferred) check weights. status.resolutionPolicy string no Latest, PinnedTag, PinnedDigest ResolutionPolicy describes how the OCI reference was resolved. Latest: unversioned ref, operator tracks the highest semver tag. PinnedTag: ref includes an explicit tag, used as-is. PinnedDigest: ref includes a digest, used as-is (immutable). Empty for inline contracts. status.resources object no Resources describes the existence of target Kubernetes resources. status.resources.service object no Service describes the target Service. status.resources.service.exists boolean yes Exists indicates whether the resource was found in the cluster. status.resources.service.kind string no Kind of the resource (only set for workloads). status.resources.service.name string yes Name of the resource. status.resources.workload object no Workload describes the target workload (Deployment/StatefulSet/ReplicaSet). status.resources.workload.exists boolean yes Exists indicates whether the resource was found in the cluster. status.resources.workload.kind string no Kind of the resource (only set for workloads). status.resources.workload.name string yes Name of the resource. status.statusFormat integer no StatusFormat is the layout this status is written in. Format 1 records interface guarantees and dependency requirements. A status without it was written by an older operator, so readers treat what it would record about them as unknown until the operator reconciles the Pacto again. status.summary object no Summary provides severity-based finding counts. status.summary.errorCount integer yes ErrorCount is the number of error-severity findings. status.summary.infoCount integer yes InfoCount is the number of info-severity findings. status.summary.unknownCount integer yes UnknownCount is the number of unknown-severity findings (a required assertion could not be evaluated). status.summary.warningCount integer yes WarningCount is the number of warning-severity findings. status.validation object no Validation describes the structural validation outcome of the contract. status.validation.errors []object no Errors lists structural validation errors. status.validation.errors[].code string no Code is a machine-readable error code. status.validation.errors[].message string yes Message is a human-readable description of the issue. status.validation.errors[].path string no Path is the JSON path to the invalid field. status.validation.valid boolean yes Valid indicates whether the contract passed structural validation. status.validation.warnings []object no Warnings lists structural validation warnings. status.validation.warnings[].code string no Code is a machine-readable error code. status.validation.warnings[].message string yes Message is a human-readable description of the issue. status.validation.warnings[].path string no Path is the JSON path to the invalid field.

docs.title: Field coverage
docs.text:
For every field you can write in a contract, this page says what checks it: pacto validate alone, a runtime check against the running service or nothing. Use it to answer "if I declare this, will Pacto notice when reality disagrees?" Each field also names the tests that prove its rule.

Runtime conformance runs three ways, and they do not see the same things: the Kubernetes operator also reads the cluster API, while pacto agent and pacto run see only the host. Every runtime-checked field says, per way, whether its evidence is verified, partial or unverified and why.

The page is generated from pkg/validation/schema/field-coverage.yaml. pkg/validation/fieldcoverage_test.go fails when a schema path or enum value is missing from that file, when an entry names no schema path and when a referenced test does not exist. Paths use [] for array items.

docs.title: Runtime classes
docs.text:
Class Meaning Fields verified A runtime fact can both satisfy and contradict the declaration. 4 partial A runtime fact exists, but some values or environments stay unverified. 15 static-only Checked by pacto validate only; nothing at runtime reads it. 97 not-applicable Identity, container or open object with nothing to verify. 14

A runtime check never turns "could not look" into a violation. A check with no usable fact is listed in status.evaluationCoverage.unverified and leaves the contract status unchanged.

docs.text: Key Value Meaning Contract format version; selects the JSON Schema the contract is validated against. docs.title: dependencies[]
docs.text: Key Value Meaning One dependency; required ones are runtime assertions. Runtime verified Evidence DependencyReachable from the provider Pacto's Service endpoints and, with the node agent, the latest TCP connect success and failure timestamps from the target pods to the provider, per peer address Rule a peer is positive when its latest success is within the staleness bound and not older than its latest failure, negative when its latest failure is within the bound and newer than its latest success; timestamps from before the pod started are ignored; any positive peer makes the dependency reachable, otherwise any negative peer is a windowed contradiction; zero ready provider endpoints beyond the window contradict; a kernel positive never overrides a Kubernetes negative (Insufficient); kernel silence never contradicts Outcomes Compliant; DEPENDENCY_UNREACHABLE (error, warning when optional); OBSERVATION_UNSUPPORTED when the provider is not a Pacto target; DEPENDENCY_UNDECLARED (warning) for reachable peers no entry names Limitations the provider must be a sibling Pacto target in the cluster; external services are Unsupported Tests unit: pkg/validation/evaluate_test.go:TestEvaluate_ContradictionPerDimension, pkg/validation/evaluate_test.go:TestEvaluate_UndeclaredDependency, pkg/validation/crossfield_test.go:TestValidateDependencyNamesUnique_Duplicate;
